“and I will kindle a fire in her forest,
and it will consume all her surroundings.”
Thus says Yahweh: “Go down to the house of the king of Judah and speak there this word.
And you shall say, ‘Hear the word of Yahweh, king of Judah, the one sitting on the throne of David, you and your servants and your people who are entering in these gates.

Thus says Yahweh: Do justice and righteousness, and rescue the one who has been robbed from the hand of the oppressor. And do not oppress the sojourner, the fatherless, or the widow. Do not do violence, and do not shed innocent blood in this place.
For if doing you do this word, then kings sitting for David on his throne will enter through the gates of this house, riding in the chariot and on horses, he and his servants and his people.
But if you will not hear these words, by myself I have sworn”—the declaration of Yahweh—“that this house will become a ruin.’”

For thus says Yahweh concerning the house of the king of Judah:
“You are Gilead to me,
the top of Lebanon.
But surely I will make you a wilderness,
cities not inhabited.

And I will consecrate destroyers against you,
a man and his weapons,
and they will cut down the choicest of your cedars
and cast them on the fire.
And many nations will pass by this city, and they will say, a man to his neighbor, ‘On account of what has Yahweh done thus to great this city?’
And they will say, ‘On account of the fact that they abandoned the covenant of Yahweh their God and bowed down to other gods and served them.’”
Do not weep for the dead one, and do not mourn for him. Weep to weep for the one going away, for he will not return again nor see his native land.
For thus says Yahweh concerning Shallum, the son of Josiah, king of Judah, the one reigning in the place of Josiah his father, who went out from this place: “He will not return there again.
But in the place where they exiled him, there he shall die, and he will not see this land again.”

Woe to the one building his house by unrighteousness
and his upper rooms by injustice,
who makes his neighbor work for nothing
and does not give him his wages,

the one saying, “I will build for myself a house of great measurements
and spacious upper rooms,”
and he cuts out windows for himself
and panels it with cedar
and paints it with vermilion.
Will you reign because you are competing in cedar? Did not your father eat and drink and do justice and righteousness? Then it was good for him.
He judged the cause of the poor and the needy. Then it was good. Is not this the knowledge of me?”—the declaration of Yahweh.
“But there is nothing in your eyes and your heart except upon your unjust gain, and upon the blood of the innocent to pour it out, and upon oppression and upon extortion to do them.

Therefore, thus says Yahweh concerning Jehoiakim, the son of Josiah, king of Judah:
“They will not mourn for him, saying,
‘Woe, my brother!’ and ‘Woe, sister!’
They will not mourn for him, saying,
‘Woe, master!’ and ‘Woe, his majesty!’

He will be buried with the burial of a donkey,
dragged and thrown out
beyond the gates of Jerusalem.”

Go up to Lebanon and cry out,
and give your voice in Bashan,
and cry out from Abarim,
for all your lovers are broken.

I spoke to you in your prosperity;
you said, ‘I will not hear.’
This has been your way from your youth,
for you have not heard my voice.

The wind shall shepherd all your shepherds,
and your lovers shall go into captivity.
Surely then you will be ashamed and humiliated
because of all your evil.

You who are dwelling in Lebanon,
you who are nesting in the cedars,
how you will be pitied when pangs come to you,
pain like the one giving birth!
As I live”—the declaration of Yahweh—“even if Coniah, the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a signet on my right hand, surely from there I would tear you off.

And I will give you into the hand of the ones seeking your life and into the hand of those whom you fear from their face, and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and into the hand of the Chaldeans.
And I will hurl you and your mother who bore you into another land where you were not born, and there you will die.
And to the land where they are lifting up their soul to return there, there they will not return!”

“Is this man Coniah a despised, shattered vessel?
Or is he a vessel in which there is no delight?
Why have they been hurled, he and his seed,
and thrown into a land that they did not know?”

Land, land, land,
hear the word of Yahweh!

Thus says Yahweh:
“Write down this man childless,
a man who will not prosper in his days,
for no man from his seed shall prosper,
sitting on the throne of David
and ruling again in Judah.”
“Woe to the shepherds who are destroying and scattering the sheep of my pasture!”—the declaration of Yahweh.

Therefore, thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, concerning the shepherds who are shepherding my people, “You yourselves have scattered my flock and have driven them away, and you have not attended to them. Behold, I am attending to you for the evil of your deeds”—the declaration of Yahweh.
“And I, I will gather the remnant of my flock from all the lands where I have driven them, and I will bring them back to their pasture, and they will be fruitful and multiply.
And I will raise up shepherds over them, and they will shepherd them. And they will no longer fear, and they will not be dismayed, and none will be missing”—the declaration of Yahweh.

“Behold, days are coming”—the declaration of Yahweh—“when I will raise up for David a righteous branch,
and he shall reign as king and act wisely, and he shall do justice and righteousness in the land.

In his days Judah will be saved,
and Israel will dwell in safety.
And this is his name by which he will be called:
‘Yahweh is our righteousness.’”
“Therefore, behold, days are coming”—the declaration of Yahweh—“when they will no longer say, ‘As Yahweh lives, who brought the sons of Israel up from the land of Egypt,’

but rather, ‘As Yahweh lives, who brought up and who led the offspring of the house of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands where I had driven them.’ And they will dwell in their own land.”

Concerning the prophets:
My heart is broken within me;
all my bones tremble.
I have become like a drunken man,
and like a man whom wine has overcome,
because of the face of Yahweh
and because of the face of his holy words.

For the land is full of adulterers,
for because of the face of a curse, the land mourns,
the pastures of the wilderness have dried up.
Their course is evil,
and their might is not right.

“For both prophet and priest are polluted;
even in my house I have found their evil”—the declaration of Yahweh.

“And among the prophets of Samaria, I saw an impropriety:
they prophesied by Baal
and led my people Israel astray.

And among the prophets of Jerusalem, I have seen a horrible thing:
committing adultery and walking in falsehood.
And they have strengthened the hands of evildoers,
so that no man turns back from his evil.
All of them have become to me like Sodom,
and her inhabitants, like Gomorrah.”

Therefore, thus says Yahweh of Armies concerning the prophets:
“Behold me making them eat wormwood
and making them drink water of poison,
for from the prophets of Jerusalem
pollution has gone out to all the land.”

Thus says Yahweh of Armies:
“Do not listen to the words of the prophets
who are prophesying to you.
They are deluding you;
they are speaking a vision of their own heart,
not from the mouth of Yahweh.

Saying, they say to the ones despising me,
‘Yahweh has spoken: Peace will be for you.’
And to everyone walking in the stubbornness of his heart they have said,
‘Disaster will not come upon you.’”

For who has stood in the counsel of Yahweh
and seen and heard his word?
Who has paid attention to his word and listened?

Behold, a storm of Yahweh! Wrath has gone out,
and a whirling tempest—
upon the head of the wicked it will whirl.

The nose of Yahweh will not turn back
until he has done and until he has established
the intentions of his heart.
In the latter days
you will understand it with understanding.

“I did not send the prophets,
yet they, they ran.
I did not speak to them,
yet they, they prophesied.

But if they had stood in my counsel,
then they would have caused my people to hear my words,
and they would have turned them back from their evil way
and from the evil of their deeds.”
“Am I a God from near”—the declaration of Yahweh—“and not a God from far?

Can a man hide himself in secret places so I will not see him?”—the declaration of Yahweh—
“Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?”—the declaration of Yahweh.
“I have heard what the prophets have said, the ones prophesying falsehood in my name, saying, ‘I have dreamed! I have dreamed!’
Until when will this be in the heart of the prophets, the ones prophesying falsehood and the prophets of the deceit of their heart,
the ones planning to make my people forget my name by their dreams which they recount, a man to his neighbor, just as their fathers forgot my name on account of Baal?
The prophet who has a dream with him, let him recount his dream, but the one who has my word with him, let him speak my word faithfully. What to the straw with the grain?”—the declaration of Yahweh.
“Is not my word like fire?”—the declaration of Yahweh—“and like a hammer that shatters a rock?”
“Therefore, behold me against the prophets”—the declaration of Yahweh—“the ones stealing my words, a man from his neighbor.
Behold me against the prophets”—the declaration of Yahweh—“the ones taking their tongue and declaring a declaration.

Behold me against the ones prophesying dreams of falsehood”—the declaration of Yahweh—“and they have recounted them and lead my people astray by their falsehoods and by their recklessness, yet I, I did not send them, and I did not command them. So benefiting, they will not benefit this people”—the declaration of Yahweh.
“And when this people, or a prophet, or a priest asks you, saying, ‘What is the burden of Yahweh?’—then you shall say to them, ‘What burden?’ And I will abandon you,” the declaration of Yahweh.
“And the prophet and the priest and the people who say, ‘The burden of Yahweh,’ I will punish that man and his house.
Thus you will say, a man to his neighbor and a man to his brother, ‘What has Yahweh answered?’ or ‘What has Yahweh spoken?’
But ‘the burden of Yahweh’ you shall not mention again, for the burden will be each man’s own word, for you have perverted the words of the living God, Yahweh of Armies, our God.
Thus you say to the prophet, ‘What has Yahweh answered you?’ or ‘What has Yahweh spoken?’
But if you say, ‘The burden of Yahweh,’ therefore thus says Yahweh: ‘Because you say this word, “The burden of Yahweh,” when I sent to you, saying, “You shall not say, ‘The burden of Yahweh,’
therefore, behold me, I will surely forget you and will abandon you and the city that I gave to you and to your fathers, from at my face.
And I will put upon you everlasting reproach and everlasting shame that will not be forgotten.”’”’

Yahweh showed me, and behold, two baskets of figs were set to the face of the temple of Yahweh, after Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, exiled Jeconiah, the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and the officials of Judah, and the craftsmen and the smiths from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon.
One basket had very good figs, like the first ripe figs, and one basket had very bad figs that could not be eaten from badness.
And said Yahweh to me, “What are you seeing, Jeremiah?” And I said, “Figs. The good figs are very good, and the bad ones are very bad, that they cannot be eaten from badness.”
And the word of Yahweh was to me, saying,
“Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel: Like these good figs, so I will regard the exile of Judah whom I sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans, for good.
And I will set my eyes on them for good, and I will bring them back to this land. And I will build them up and not tear them down, and I will plant them and not uproot them.
And I will give to them a heart to know me, that I am Yahweh. And they will be to me for a people, and I, I will be to them for God, for they will return to me with all of their heart.

And like the bad figs that cannot be eaten from badness”—for thus says Yahweh—“so I will give Zedekiah, king of Judah, and his officials, and the remnant of Jerusalem, the ones remaining in this land, and the ones dwelling in the land of Egypt.
And I will give them to horror, for evil, to all of the kingdoms of the earth, for a reproach and for a proverb, for a taunt and for a curse, in all of the places where I will drive them there.
And I will send among them the sword, the famine, and the plague, until they are consumed from upon the land that I gave to them and to their fathers.”
The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all of the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the son of Josiah, king of Judah—that was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—
which Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all of the people of Judah and to all of the dwellers of Jerusalem, saying,

“From the thirteenth year of Josiah, son of Amon, king of Judah, and until this day—this is twenty-three years—the word of Yahweh has come to me, and I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, but you have not listened.
And Yahweh has sent to you all of his servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, but you have not listened, and you have not extended your ear to hear,
saying, ‘Turn back, please, each man from his evil way and from the evil of your deeds, and dwell on the land that Yahweh gave to you and to your fathers from everlasting to everlasting.
And do not go after other gods to serve them and to bow down to them, and do not provoke me to anger with the work of your hands, and I will not do harm to you.’
Yet you have not listened to me”—the declaration of Yahweh—“so as to provoke me to anger with the work of your hands, to your harm.
Therefore, thus says Yahweh of Armies, ‘Because you have not listened to my words,

behold me sending, and I will take all of the families of the north”—the declaration of Yahweh—“and to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I will bring them against this land and against its dwellers and against all of these nations all around, and I will devote them to destruction and will make them a horror and a hissing and to an eternal desolation.
And I will cause to perish from them the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the sound of the bridegroom and the sound of the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp.
And all of this land will become a ruin, a desolation, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

And it will happen, when seventy years are fulfilled, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation”—the declaration of Yahweh—“for their iniquity, and the land of the Chaldeans, and I will make it a perpetual desolation.
And I will bring upon that land all of my words that I have spoken against it, all of that which is written in this book, which Jeremiah has prophesied against all of the nations.
For many nations and great kings will also make them serve, even them, and I will repay them according to their deed and according to the work of their hands.’”
For thus says Yahweh, God of Israel, to me, “Take this cup of the wine of the wrath from my hand, and you will make all of the nations to which I am sending you drink it.
And they will drink and will stagger and will act like madmen from the face of the sword that I am sending among them.”
And I took the cup from the hand of Yahweh, and I made all of the nations drink, those to which Yahweh had sent me:
Jerusalem and the cities of Judah and its kings and its officials, to make them a ruin, a desolation, a hissing, and a curse, as on this day;
Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and his servants and his officials and all of his people,
and all of the mixed people, and all of the kings of the land of Uz, and all of the kings of the land of the Philistines—Ashkelon and Gaza and Ekron and the remnant of Ashdod;
Edom and Moab and the sons of Ammon;
and all of the kings of Tyre and all of the kings of Sidon and the kings of the coastland that is across the sea;
and Dedan and Tema and Buz and all of the ones cut off at the corner;
and all of the kings of Arabia and all of the kings of the mixed people who dwell in the wilderness;
and all of the kings of Zimri and all of the kings of Elam and all of the kings of Media;
and all of the kings of the north, the near and the far, a man to his brother, and all of the kingdoms of the world that are on the face of the earth. And the king of Sheshach shall drink after them.
“Then you shall say to them, ‘Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: Drink and be drunk and vomit and fall, and do not rise, from the face of the sword that I am sending among you.’
And it will happen, if they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink, then you shall say to them, ‘Thus says Yahweh of Armies: Drinking, you shall drink.’

For behold, in the city over which my name is called I am beginning to bring harm, and you, being acquitted, will you be acquitted? You will not be acquitted, for a sword I am calling against all of the dwellers of the earth”—the declaration of Yahweh of Armies.

“And you, you will prophesy to them all of these words and say to them,
‘Yahweh will roar from the height,
and from the habitation of his holiness, he will give his voice.
Roaring, he will roar against his pasture;
a shout like those who are treading, he will sing
to all of the dwellers of the earth.

A tumult will come to the end of the earth,
for Yahweh has a dispute with the nations.
He is entering into judgment with all flesh;
the wicked—he will give them to the sword’”—the declaration of Yahweh.

Thus says Yahweh of Armies,
“Behold, disaster is going out from nation to nation,
and a great storm will be stirred up
from the farthest parts of the earth.

And the slain of Yahweh shall be on that day
from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth.
They shall not be mourned,
and they shall not be gathered, and they shall not be buried.
They will be as dung on the face of the ground.

Wail, you shepherds, and cry out,
and roll in the dust, you nobles of the flock,
for your days for slaughter and your dispersions have been fulfilled,
and you shall fall like a vessel of delight.

And refuge shall vanish from the shepherds,
and escape, from the noble ones of the flock.

There is the sound of the cry of the shepherds
and the wailing of the nobles of the flock,
for Yahweh is destroying their pasture.

And the pastures of peace are devastated
from the face of the burning of the nose of Yahweh.

He has left his lair like the young lion,
for their land has become a desolation
from the face of the burning of the oppressor
and from the face of the burning of his nose.”
In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim, the son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word was from Yahweh, saying,

“Thus says Yahweh: Stand in the courtyard of the house of Yahweh and speak to all the cities of Judah that are coming to bow down in the house of Yahweh all the words that I have commanded you to speak to them. Do not take away a word.
Perhaps they will listen and turn back, a man from his evil way. Then I will relent concerning the disaster that I am planning to do to them from the face of the evil of their deeds.”
And you shall say to them, “Thus says Yahweh: ‘If you do not listen to me, to walk in my law that I have given to the face of you,
to listen to the words of my servants the prophets whom I am sending to you, rising early and sending, but you have not listened,
then I will make this house like Shiloh, and this city I will make as a curse for all the nations of the earth.’”
And the priests and the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of Yahweh.

And it happened, when Jeremiah had finished speaking all that Yahweh had commanded him to speak to all the people, that the priests and the prophets and all the people seized him, saying, “Dying, you must die!

Why have you prophesied in the name of Yahweh, saying, ‘Like Shiloh this house will be, and this city will be desolate, without a dweller’?” And all the people gathered against Jeremiah in the house of Yahweh.
And the officials of Judah heard these things, and they went up from the house of the king to the house of Yahweh, and they sat down in the entrance of the New Gate of Yahweh.

And the priests and the prophets said to the officials and to all the people, saying, “A judgment of death to this man, because he has prophesied against this city, just as you have heard with your ears.”
And Jeremiah said to all the officials and to all the people, saying, “Yahweh sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city all the words that you have heard.
And now, make good your ways and your deeds, and listen to the voice of Yahweh your God, and Yahweh will relent concerning the disaster that he has spoken against you.
And as for me, behold me in your hand. Do to me according to the good and according to the right in your eyes.

Only, knowing, you will know that if you are putting me to death, then you are putting innocent blood upon yourselves and upon this city and upon its dwellers, for in truth Yahweh has sent me to you to speak in your ears all these words.”
And the officials and all the people said to the priests and to the prophets, “There is no judgment of death for this man, for in the name of Yahweh our God he has spoken to us.”
And men from the elders of the land rose up and said to all the assembly of the people, saying,

“Micah the Morashtite was prophesying in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and he said to all the people of Judah, saying, ‘Thus says Yahweh of Armies:
Zion, a field will be plowed,
and Jerusalem will become heaps,
and the mountain of the house to high places of a forest.’

Putting to death, did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Did he not fear Yahweh and entreat the face of Yahweh, and Yahweh relented concerning the evil that he had spoken against them? But we are doing great evil against ourselves.”

And also there was a man prophesying in the name of Yahweh, Uriah, the son of Shemaiah, from Kiriath Jearim, and he prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah.
And King Jehoiakim and all his mighty men and all the officials heard his words, and the king sought to put him to death. And Uriah heard, and he was afraid, and he fled and went to Egypt.
And King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt -- Elnathan, the son of Akbor, and men with him -- to Egypt.
And they brought Uriah out from Egypt, and they brought him to King Jehoiakim, and he struck him with the sword and threw his corpse into the graves of the sons of the people.
However, the hand of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, was with Jeremiah so as not to give him into the hand of the people to put him to death.
In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim, the son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word was to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,

footnotes.text: Although the Hebrew text reads “Jehoiakim,” the context of this chapter indicates that this prophecy occurred during the reign of Zedekiah.

verses.text: “Thus says Yahweh to me, ‘Make for yourself bonds and yoke bars, and put them on your neck.

And send them to the king of Edom, and to the king of Moab, and to the king of the sons of Ammon, and to the king of Tyre, and to the king of Sidon, by the hand of the messengers who are coming to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.
And command them to their masters, saying, “Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: Thus you shall say to your masters,
‘I myself made the earth, the man and the beast that are on the face of the earth, by my great strength and by my outstretched arm, and I have given it to whoever is right in my eyes.
And now I myself have given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant. And also the animal of the field I have given to him to serve him.
And all the nations will serve him and his son and the son of his son, until the time of his own land comes, even it. And many nations and great kings will make him serve them.

And it shall be that the nation and the kingdom that will not serve him, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and that will not put its neck in the yoke of the king of Babylon, with the sword and with the famine and with the plague, I will visit upon that nation”—the declaration of Yahweh—“until I have finished them by his hand.

And as for you, do not listen to your prophets, and to your diviners, and to your dreamers, and to your soothsayers, and to your sorcerers, they who are speaking to you, saying, ‘You shall not serve the king of Babylon.’
For they are prophesying falsehood to you, so as to remove you far away from on your land, and I will drive you out, and you will perish.
But the nation that brings its neck into the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, I will let it rest on its land”—the declaration of Yahweh—“and it will cultivate it and dwell in it.’”’”
And to Zedekiah, king of Judah, I spoke according to all these words, saying, “Bring your necks into the yoke of the king of Babylon and serve him and his people, and live.
Why will you die, you and your people, by the sword, by the famine, and by the plague, as Yahweh has spoken concerning the nation that does not serve the king of Babylon?
And do not listen to the words of the prophets who are speaking to you, saying, ‘You shall not serve the king of Babylon,’ for they are prophesying falsehood to you.

For I have not sent them”—the declaration of Yahweh—“and they are prophesying in my name for falsehood, so that I will drive you out, and you will perish, you and the prophets who are prophesying to you.”

And to the priests and to all this people I spoke, saying, “Thus says Yahweh: Do not listen to the words of your prophets who are prophesying to you, saying, ‘Behold, the vessels of the house of Yahweh are being brought back from Babylon now, quickly,’ for they are prophesying falsehood to you.
Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon and live. Why should this city become a ruin?

And if they are prophets, and if the word of Yahweh is with them, let them please intercede with Yahweh of Armies, that the vessels remaining in the house of Yahweh and in the house of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem not go to Babylon.”
For thus says Yahweh of Armies concerning the pillars, and concerning the Sea, and concerning the stands, and concerning the rest of the vessels remaining in this city,
which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he exiled Jeconiah, the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, from Jerusalem to Babylon, and all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem—
for thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, concerning the vessels remaining in the house of Yahweh and the house of the king of Judah and Jerusalem:
“They will be brought to Babylon, and there they will be until the day of my visiting them”—the declaration of Yahweh—“and I will bring them up and restore them to this place.”

Now it happened in that year, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, Hananiah, the son of Azzur, the prophet who was from Gibeon, said to me in the house of Yahweh, to the eyes of the priests and all the people, saying,
“Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, saying, ‘I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within two years of days, I myself am bringing back to this place all the vessels of the house of Yahweh that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from this place and brought them to Babylon.

And I myself am bringing back to this place Jeconiah, the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the exile of Judah, the ones going to Babylon’—the declaration of Yahweh—‘for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.’”
And Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the prophet, to the eyes of the priests and to the eyes of all the people, the ones standing in the house of Yahweh,

and Jeremiah the prophet said, “Amen! Thus may Yahweh do! May Yahweh establish your words that you prophesied, to bring back the vessels of the house of Yahweh and all the exiles from Babylon to this place.
But please hear this word that I myself am speaking in your ears and in the ears of all the people:
The prophets who were to the face of me and to the face of you from ancient time, they prophesied to many lands and against great kingdoms, regarding war and regarding disaster and regarding plague.
The prophet who prophesies of peace, when the word of the prophet comes, the prophet will be known as one whom Yahweh has sent in truth.”
And Hananiah the prophet took the yoke bar from upon the neck of Jeremiah the prophet and broke it.

And Hananiah said to the eyes of all the people, saying, “Thus says Yahweh: ‘Like this I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon within two more years of days from upon the neck of all the nations.’” And Jeremiah the prophet went on his way.
And the word of Yahweh was to Jeremiah after Hananiah the prophet broke the yoke bar from upon the neck of Jeremiah the prophet, saying,
“Go, and you shall speak to Hananiah, saying, ‘Thus says Yahweh: You have broken yoke bars of wood, but you will make in their place yoke bars of iron.’

For thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: ‘I have put a yoke of iron on the neck of all these nations to serve Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and they will serve him. And also the animal of the field I have given to him.’”
And Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the prophet, “Listen, please, Hananiah! Yahweh has not sent you, and you yourself have made this people trust in falsehood.
Therefore, thus says Yahweh: ‘Behold me sending you away from upon the face of the earth. This year you are dying, for you have spoken rebellion against Yahweh.’”
And Hananiah the prophet died in that year, in the seventh month.

And these are the words of the scroll that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the remainder of the elders of the exile, and to the priests, and to the prophets, and to all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had exiled from Jerusalem to Babylon,
after the going out of Jeconiah the king, and the queen mother, and the eunuchs, the princes of Judah and Jerusalem, and the craftsmen and the smiths, from Jerusalem.
He sent it by the hand of Elasah, the son of Shaphan, and Gemariah, the son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah the king of Judah sent to Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, to Babylon, saying,
“Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, to all the exile whom I have exiled from Jerusalem to Babylon:
‘Build houses and dwell in them, and plant gardens and eat their fruit.
Take wives, and father sons and daughters, and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to men, that they may bear sons and daughters, and multiply there, and you not become few.
And seek the peace of the city where I have exiled you there, and pray on behalf of it to Yahweh, for in its peace there shall be peace for you.’

For thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: ‘Let your prophets who are in your midst and your diviners not deceive you, and do not listen to your dreams that you are causing yourselves to dream.
For in falsehood they are prophesying to you in my name. I did not send them’—the declaration of Yahweh.
For thus says Yahweh: ‘When is completed seventy years for Babylon, I will visit you, and I will establish my good word concerning you, to bring you back to this place.
For I myself know the plans that I am planning concerning you’—the declaration of Yahweh—‘plans of peace and not for evil, to give to you a future and a hope.
And you will call to me and will go and pray to me, and I will listen to you.
And you will seek me and will find me, when you seek me with all your heart.

And I will be found by you’—the declaration of Yahweh—‘and I will return your restoration and I will gather you from all the nations and from all the places where I have driven you there’—the declaration of Yahweh—‘and I will bring you back to the place from where I exiled you.’
Because you have said, ‘Yahweh has raised up prophets for us in Babylon’—
for thus says Yahweh concerning the king who is sitting on the throne of David and concerning all the people who are dwelling in this city, your brothers who did not go out with you into the exile—
thus says Yahweh of Armies: ‘Behold me sending against them the sword, the famine, and the plague, and I will make them like the horrible figs that cannot be eaten from badness.

And I will pursue after them with the sword, with the famine, and with the plague, and I will make them to be a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a curse and a desolation and a hissing and a reproach among all the nations where I have driven them,
because they did not listen to my words“—the declaration of Yahweh—“that I sent to them by my servants the prophets, rising early and sending, but you did not listen“—the declaration of Yahweh.
“But you, hear the word of Yahweh, all the exile whom I have sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.

Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, concerning Ahab, the son of Kolaiah, and concerning Zedekiah, the son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying to you in my name falsehood: ‘Behold me giving them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, and he will strike them before your eyes.
And because of them a curse shall be taken up by all the exile of Judah who are in Babylon, saying, “May Yahweh make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire,”

because they have done a shameful thing in Israel, and they have committed adultery with the wives of their neighbors, and they spoke a word in my name falsely that I did not command them. And I am the one knowing and am a witness’—the declaration of Yahweh.”
And to Shemaiah, the Nehelamite, you shall speak, saying,

“Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, saying: ‘Because you sent letters in your name to all the people who are in Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah, the son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,

“Yahweh has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be overseers in the house of Yahweh over every man who is raving and making himself a prophet, and you shall put him in the stocks and in the neck iron.
And now, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah, the Anathothite, the one making himself a prophet to you?
For on account of this, he has sent to us in Babylon, saying, ‘It will be long. Build houses and dwell in them, and plant gardens and eat their fruit.’”’”
And Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the ears of Jeremiah the prophet.
And the word of Yahweh was to Jeremiah, saying,
“Send to all the exile, saying, ‘Thus says Yahweh concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you, and I did not send him, and he made you trust upon falsehood,

therefore, thus says Yahweh: Behold me visiting punishment upon Shemaiah the Nehelamite and upon his seed. There will not be for him a man dwelling in the midst of this people, and he will not see the good that I am doing for my people’—the declaration of Yahweh—‘for he has spoken rebellion against Yahweh.’”
The word that was to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,
“Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, saying, ‘Write for yourself in a scroll all of the words that I have spoken to you.

For behold, days are coming“—the declaration of Yahweh—“when I will restore the captivity of my people Israel and Judah,” says Yahweh, “and I will bring them back to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they will possess it.’”
And these are the words that Yahweh spoke concerning Israel and to Judah.

For thus says Yahweh,
“We have heard a voice of trembling,
dread, and there is no peace.

Ask, please, and see,
can a male be giving birth?
Why do I see every strong man
with his hands on his loins
like a woman giving birth?
And all of the faces have turned
to paleness.

Woe! For great is that day,
there is none like it.
And it is a time of distress for Jacob,
but he will be saved from it.
And it will be on that day“—the declaration of Yahweh of Armies—“I will break his yoke from upon your neck, and I will tear apart your bonds, and foreigners will no longer enslave him.
And they will serve Yahweh their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.

And you, my servant Jacob, do not fear”—the declaration of Yahweh—“and do not be dismayed, Israel, for behold me saving you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity. And Jacob shall return and shall have quiet and shall be at ease, and there shall be no one making him afraid.

For I am with you”—the declaration of Yahweh—“to save you. For I will make a complete end of all of the nations where I have scattered you, but you I will not make a complete end of. And I will discipline you according to justice, but acquitting, I will not acquit you.”

For thus says Yahweh, “Incurable is your breaking;
grievous is your wound.

Why do you cry out over your breaking,
your pain that is incurable?
Because of the abundance of your iniquity,
your sins are numerous,
I have done these things to you.

Therefore, all of the ones devouring you will be devoured,
and all of your adversaries, every one of them,
will go into captivity.
And the ones plundering you will be as plunder,
and all of the ones preying upon you I will give as prey.

For I will bring up healing for you,
and I will heal you from your wounds”—
the declaration of Yahweh—
“for they have called you an outcast:
‘She is Zion; no one is seeking her.’”

Thus says Yahweh, “Behold me returning the restoration of the tents of Jacob,
and I will have compassion on his dwelling places.
And the city shall be built on its mound,
and the palace shall sit on its proper place.

And thanksgiving will go out from them,
and the voice of those laughing.
And I will multiply them, and they will not become few,
and I will make them honored, and they will not become insignificant.

And his sons will be as in former times,
and his congregation will be established to my face,
and I will visit all of his oppressors.

And his majestic one will be from among him,
and his ruler will come from his midst.
And I will bring him near, and he will approach me,
for who is this who has pledged his heart
to approach me?”—
the declaration of Yahweh.

“And you will be to me for a people,
and I will be to you for God.”

Behold, the storm of Yahweh,
wrath, has gone out,
a whirling storm;
upon the head of the wicked it will whirl.

The burning of the nose of Yahweh will not turn back
until his doing and until his establishing
the plans of his heart.
In the latter days,
you will understand it.
“At that time”—the declaration of Yahweh—“I will be for God to all of the clans of Israel, and they will be my people.”
Thus says Yahweh, “A people, the survivors of the sword, found favor in the wilderness, Israel, going to find his rest.”

From far off Yahweh appeared to me, “And with everlasting love I have loved you.
Therefore I have drawn you out with covenant faithfulness.

Again I will build you, and you will be built, virgin of Israel.
Again you will adorn yourself with your tambourines, and you will go out in the dance of the ones laughing.

Again you will plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria;
the planters will plant and will treat them as common.

For there will be a day when the watchers on the mountain of Ephraim will call out,
‘Arise, and let us go up to Zion, to Yahweh our God.’”
For thus says Yahweh, “Sing for Jacob with gladness, and shout for the chief of the nations. Cause it to be heard, praise, and say, ‘Yahweh, save your people, the remnant of Israel.’

Behold me bringing them from the land of the north, and I will gather them from the remote parts of the earth. Among them are the blind and the lame, the pregnant woman and the one giving birth, together; a great assembly will return here.

With weeping they will come, and with pleas for mercy I will lead them. I will cause them to walk to streams of water on a straight road; they will not stumble on it. For I have become a father for Israel, and Ephraim, he is my firstborn.
Hear the word of Yahweh, nations, and declare it in the coastlands from far off, and say, ‘The one scattering Israel will gather him, and he will protect him like a shepherd of his flock.’
For Yahweh has ransomed Jacob and redeemed him from the hand of one stronger than he.

And they will come and will sing on the height of Zion, and they will be radiant to the goodness of Yahweh, over the grain, and over the new wine, and over the fresh oil, and over the young of the flock and the herd. And their soul will be like a watered garden, and they will not continue to languish again.
Then the virgin will rejoice with dancing, and the young men and the old together. And I will turn their mourning to joy, and I will comfort them, and I will cause them to rejoice rather than sorrow.
And I will saturate the soul of the priests with fatness, and my people will be satisfied with my goodness— the declaration of Yahweh.
Thus says Yahweh, “A voice is heard in Ramah, wailing, the weeping of bitterness. Rachel is weeping over her sons; she refuses to be comforted over her sons, for he is no more.”
Thus says Yahweh, “Withhold your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your work”—the declaration of Yahweh—“and they will return from the land of the enemy.
And there is hope for your future”—the declaration of Yahweh—“and will return your sons to their border.
Hearing, I have heard Ephraim bemoaning himself, ‘You disciplined me, and I was disciplined like a calf not trained. Cause me to return, and I will return, for you are Yahweh my God.
For after my turning away, I repented, and after my being made to know, I struck on my thigh. I was ashamed, and also I was humiliated, for I bore the reproach of my youth.’

Is Ephraim a precious son to me, or a child of delights? For as often as I speak against him, remembering, I remember him. still Therefore my inward parts groan for him; having compassion, I will have compassion on him”—the declaration of Yahweh.
Set up for yourself signposts; place for yourself markers. Set your heart to the highway, the road you walked. Return, virgin of Israel; return to these, your cities.
Until when will you waver, apostate daughter? For Yahweh has created a new thing in the land: a female will surround a man protectively.”

Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, “Again they will say this word in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I return their restoration, ‘May Yahweh bless you, dwelling place of righteousness, mountain of holiness.’
And in it Judah and all its cities together will dwell, farmers and those who set out with the flock.
For I will saturate the weary soul, and every languishing soul I will fill.”
At this, I awoke and looked, and my sleep was pleasant to me.
“Behold, days are coming”—the declaration of Yahweh—“when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and the seed of beast.

And it will be, just as I watched over them to uproot and to tear down, and to overthrow and to destroy and to bring harm, thus I will watch over them to build and to plant”—the declaration of Yahweh.

In those days they will no longer say,
‘Fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children will become blunt.’
But a man will die in his own iniquity; every man who eats the sour grapes, his teeth will become blunt.
Behold, days are coming”—the declaration of Yahweh—“when I will cut a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.

It will not be like the covenant that I cut with their fathers on the day of my taking hold of their hand to bring them out from the land of Egypt, which they, they broke—my covenant—although I was a husband to them”—the declaration of Yahweh.

For this is the covenant that I will cut with the house of Israel after those days—the declaration of Yahweh: I will put my law in their inward parts, and on their heart I will write it; and I will be God for them, and they will be a people for me.

And no longer will a man teach his neighbor and a man, his brother, saying, ‘Know Yahweh,’ for all of them will know me from the smallest of them to the greatest of them”—the declaration of Yahweh—“for I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will no longer remember.”

Thus says Yahweh, the one giving the sun for light by day, the statutes of the moon and the stars for light by night, the one stirring up the sea, its waves, so that roar, Yahweh of Armies is his name:
“If these statutes depart from before me”—the declaration of Yahweh—“then also the seed of Israel will cease from being a nation before me all the days.”

Thus says Yahweh, “If the heavens above can be measured and can be searched out, the foundations of the earth below, then also I, I will reject all the seed of Israel for all that they have done”—the declaration of Yahweh.
“Behold, days are coming”—the declaration of Yahweh—“when the city will be built for Yahweh, from the Tower of Hananel to the Gate of the Corner.
And will go out the measuring line again straight over the hill of Gareb, and then turn toward Goah.

And all the valley of the corpses and the ashes, and all the fields as far as the brook of Kidron, to the corner of the Gate of the Horses toward the east, will be holiness to Yahweh. It will not be uprooted, and it will not be overthrown again forever.”
The word that was to Jeremiah from Yahweh in the tenth year of Zedekiah the king of Judah—that was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
And at that time the army of the king of Babylon was laying siege to Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the courtyard of the guard that was in the house of the king of Judah,
where Zedekiah the king of Judah had shut him up, saying, “Why are you prophesying, saying, ‘Thus says Yahweh: Behold me giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

And Zedekiah the king of Judah will not escape from the hand of the Chaldeans, for being given, he will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and his mouth will speak with his mouth, and his eyes will see his eyes.
And he will make Zedekiah go to Babylon, and there he will be until I visit him”—the declaration of Yahweh—“though you fight against the Chaldeans, you will not succeed’?”
And Jeremiah said, “The word of Yahweh was to me, saying,
‘Behold, Hanamel the son of Shallum your uncle is coming to you, saying, “Buy for yourself my field that is in Anathoth, for to you belongs the right of redemption, to buy it.”’

And Hanamel, the son of my uncle, came to me, according to the word of Yahweh, to the courtyard of the guard, and he said to me, ‘Buy, please, my field that is in Anathoth, which is in the land of Benjamin, for to you belongs the right of possession, and to you, the redemption. Buy it for yourself.’ Then I knew that this was the word of Yahweh.
So I bought the field from Hanamel, the son of my uncle, which was in Anathoth, and I weighed out for him the silver, seven shekels and ten of the silver.
And I wrote in the document and sealed it, and I caused to testify witnesses, and I weighed the silver on the scales.
Then I took the document of the purchase—the one being sealed, the commandment and the terms, and the one being open—

and I gave the document of the purchase to Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, before the eyes of Hanamel of my uncle and before the eyes of the witnesses, the ones signing on the document of the purchase, before the eyes of all the Judeans who were sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
And I commanded Baruch before their eyes, saying,

‘Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: Take these documents, this document of the purchase, both the sealed one and this open document, and put them in a vessel of earthenware, so that they may stand many days.
For thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: Houses and fields and vineyards will again be bought in this land.’
And I prayed to Yahweh after I gave the document of the purchase to Baruch, the son of Neriah, saying,
Ah, Lord Yahweh! Behold you, you made the heavens and the earth by your great power and by your outstretched arm. Nothing is too difficult for you,
doing covenant faithfulness to thousands and repaying the iniquity of fathers into the bosom of their sons after them, the great and mighty God—Yahweh of Armies is his name—
great in counsel and abounding in deed, whose eyes are open to all of the ways of the sons of man, to give to each according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds,
who have set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, until this day, and in Israel and among mankind, and you made for yourself a name, as at this day.
And you brought out your people Israel from the land of Egypt with signs and with wonders and with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm and with great terror.
And you gave to them this land, which you swore to their fathers to give to them, a land flowing with milk and honey.

And they entered and took possession of it, but they did not listen to your voice, and in your law they did not walk. All that you commanded them to do, they have not done, and so you caused all this calamity to happen to them.

Behold, the siege mounds have come to the city to capture it, and the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans who are fighting against it, because of the face of the sword and the famine and the plague. And what you spoke has happened, and behold, you are seeing it.
Yet you, you said to me, Lord Yahweh, “Buy for yourself the field with silver and cause witnesses to testify,” though the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans.’”
And the word of Yahweh was to Jeremiah, saying,
“Behold, I am Yahweh, the God of all flesh. Is anything too difficult for me?
Therefore, thus says Yahweh: Behold me giving this city into the hand of the Chaldeans and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

And the Chaldeans who are fighting against this city will come, and they will set this city on fire and they will burn it and the houses on whose roofs they made smoke to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods so as to provoke me.

For the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah have only been doing evil in my eyes from their youth, for the sons of Israel have surely been provoking me with the work of their hands”—the declaration of Yahweh.
For this city has been to me to my nose and to my heat from the day that they built it and until this day, so that I should remove it from by my face,

because of all the evil of the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah that they did to provoke me to anger—they, their kings, their officials, their priests, and their prophets, and the men of Judah and the dwellers of Jerusalem.
And they turned to me the neck and not the face, and though teaching them, rising early and teaching, but they were not listening to receive instruction.
And they set their detestable things in the house which my name is called over, to defile it.

And they built the high places of Baal that are in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, to make their sons and their daughters pass through to Molech, which I did not command them, and it did not come up to my heart to do this abomination, so as to cause Judah to sin.

And now, therefore, thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, concerning this city about which you are saying, ‘It has been given into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword and by the famine and by the plague’:
Behold me gathering them from all the lands where I drove them there in my anger and in my heat and in great fury, and I will bring them back to this place and cause them to dwell in security.
And they will be my people, and I myself will be their God.
And I will give to them one heart and one way, to fear me all the days, for good to them and to their sons after them.
And I will cut for them an everlasting covenant that I will not turn back from after them, to do good to them, and I will put my fear in their heart, so that they will not turn aside from by me.
And I will rejoice over them to do good to them, and I will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all my heart and with all my being.
For thus says Yahweh: Just as I brought to this people all this great calamity, so I am bringing upon them all the good that I am speaking concerning them.
And the field will be bought in this land about which you are saying, “It is a desolation, without man and beast; it has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans.”

They will buy fields with the silver and writing in the document and sealing and making witnesses witness in the land of Benjamin and in the surroundings of Jerusalem and in the cities of Judah and in the cities of the hill country and in the cities of the foothills and in the cities of the Negev, for I will restore their restoration”—the declaration of Yahweh.
And the word of Yahweh was to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still confined in the courtyard of the guard, saying,
“Thus says Yahweh its maker, Yahweh forming it to establish it—Yahweh is his name:
‘Call to me, and I will answer you, and I will declare to you great things and inaccessible things that you have not known.’
For thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, concerning the houses of this city and concerning the houses of the kings of Judah that are torn down against the siege ramps and against the sword:

‘They are coming to fight with the Chaldeans and to fill them with the corpses of the man whom in my nose and in my heat I will strike, and whom I have hidden my face from this city on account of all their wickedness.
Behold me bringing up for it healing and a cure, and I will heal them, and I will reveal to them an abundance of peace and truth.
And I will restore the restoration of Judah and the restoration of Israel, and I will build them as at the first.
And I will cleanse them from all their iniquity that they have sinned against me, and I will forgive all their iniquities that they have sinned against me and by which they transgressed against me.

And it will be for me a name of joy, for praise, and for glory before all the nations of the earth who will hear of all the good that I am doing for them. And they will fear and tremble over all the good and over all the peace that I am doing for it.’

Thus says Yahweh: ‘Again there will be heard in this place—about which you are saying, “It is a waste, without man and without beast”—in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem that are desolate, without man and without inhabitant and without beast,

the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of the ones saying, “Give thanks to Yahweh of Armies, for Yahweh is good, for his covenant faithfulness is forever,” the ones bringing thanksgiving to the house of Yahweh. For I will restore the restoration of the land as at the first,’ says Yahweh.
Thus says Yahweh of Armies: ‘Again there will be in this place, the desolate one—without man and without beast—and in all its cities a pasture of shepherds causing their flock to lie down.

In the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the foothills, and in the cities of the Negev, and in the land of Benjamin, and in the surroundings of Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, again the flock will pass under the hands of the one counting them,’ says Yahweh.
Behold, days are coming”—the declaration of Yahweh—“when I will establish the good word that I spoke to the house of Israel and to the house of Judah.
In those days and in that time I will cause to sprout for David a branch of righteousness, and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved, and Jerusalem will dwell in security, and this is what one will call her: “Yahweh is our righteousness.”
For thus says Yahweh: ‘A man will not be cut off for David sitting on the throne of the house of Israel,
nor will the priests, the Levites, a man will not be cut off from before my face, raising a burnt offering, and burning a grain offering, and making a sacrifice all the days.’”
And the word of Yahweh came to Jeremiah, saying,
“Thus says Yahweh: ‘If you break my covenant of the day and my covenant of the night, so that day and night do not come in their time,
then also my covenant will be broken with David my servant, from there being for him a son reigning on his throne, and with the Levites, the priests, my ministers.
As the host of the heavens cannot be counted, and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the seed of David my servant and the Levites, the ones ministering to me.’”
And the word of Yahweh was to Jeremiah, saying,

“Have you not seen what this people has spoken, saying, ‘The two families that Yahweh chose in them, now he has rejected them’? Thus they despise my people from being a nation anymore before their face.
Thus says Yahweh: ‘If I have not established my covenant of day and night, and if I have not set the statutes of heaven and earth,

then also the seed of Jacob and David my servant I will reject, from taking rulers from his seed over the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For I will return their restoration and I will have compassion on them.’”

The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army and all the kingdoms of the earth, the dominion of his hand, and all the peoples were fighting against Jerusalem and against all her cities, saying:

“Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel: Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah and say to him, ‘Thus says Yahweh: Behold me giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.

And you, you will not escape from his hand, but capturing you will be captured, and into his hand you will be given. And your eyes will see the eyes of the king of Babylon, and his mouth will speak with your mouth, and to Babylon you will go.’
Yet hear the word of Yahweh, Zedekiah king of Judah! Thus says Yahweh concerning you: ‘You will not die by the sword.

In peace you will die, and like the burnings of your fathers, the former kings who were before you, so they will burn for you, “Alas, master!” they will mourn for you, for I myself have spoken a word—the declaration of Yahweh.’”
And Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Zedekiah king of Judah all these words in Jerusalem,

while the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against all the remaining cities of Judah, against Lachish and against Azekah, for these remained among the cities of Judah as cities of fortification.
The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh after King Zedekiah cut a covenant with all the people who were in Jerusalem, to proclaim freedom to them,
to send away, a man his male servant and a man his female servant, the Hebrew man and the Hebrew woman, free, to not serve by them—on a Jew, his brother man.

And all the officials and all the people who had entered into the covenant obeyed—to send away, a man his male servant and a man his female servant, free, to not serve by them any longer—and they obeyed and sent them away.
But afterward they turned back and brought back the male servants and the female servants whom they had sent away free, and they subjected them as male servants and as female servants.
And the word of Yahweh came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying:
“Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel: I, I cut a covenant with your fathers in the day of my bringing them out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves, saying,

‘At the end of seven years you shall send away a man his brother, the Hebrew who has been sold to you and has served you six years, then you shall send him away free from you.’ But your fathers did not listen to me, and they did not incline their ear.
And you, you turned today and did what is right in my eyes, to proclaim freedom, a man to his neighbor, and you cut a covenant to my face, in the house over which my name is called.

But you turned and profaned my name, and you brought back, a man his male servant and a man his female servant whom you had sent away free for themselves, and you subjected them to be for you for male servants and for female servants.

Therefore thus says Yahweh: You, you have not listened to me to proclaim freedom, a man to his brother and a man to his neighbor. Behold me proclaiming freedom to you”—the declaration of Yahweh—“to the sword, to the plague, and to the famine, and I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
And I will give the men transgressing my covenant, who did not establish the words of the covenant that they cut before my face—the calf that they cut in two and passed between its pieces—
the officials of Judah and the officials of Jerusalem, the eunuchs and the priests, and all the people of the land, the ones passing between the pieces of the calf—
and I will give them into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of the ones seeking their life, and their corpse will be as food for the bird of the heavens and for the beast of the earth.

And Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials I will give into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of the ones seeking their life, and into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, the ones withdrawing from against you.

Behold me, commanding,”—the declaration of Yahweh—“and I will bring them back to this city, and they will fight against it and capture it and burn it with fire. And the cities of Judah I will make a desolation, without inhabitant.”
The word that was to Jeremiah from Yahweh in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying,
“Go to the house of the Rechabites and speak with them, and bring them to the house of Yahweh, into one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink.”
So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah son of Habazziniah, and his brothers, and all his sons, and all the house of the Rechabites,

and I brought them to the house of Yahweh, into the chamber of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God, which was beside the chamber of the officials, which was above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the threshold.
Then I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites bowls full of wine, and cups, and I said to them, “Drink wine.”
But they said, “We will not drink wine, for Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying, ‘You shall not drink wine, you nor your sons, forever.

And you shall not build a house, and you shall not sow seed, and you shall not plant a vineyard, and it shall not be to you; but in tents you shall dwell all your days, so that you may live many days on the face of the earth where you are sojourning there.’
And we have listened to the voice of Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, in all that he commanded us, to not drink wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters,
and to not build houses for us to inhabit, and there will not be to us vineyard or field or seed.
But we have dwelt in tents, and we have listened and done according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us.

But it happened, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against the land, that we said, ‘Come, and let us go to Jerusalem from before the face of the army of the Chaldeans and from before the face of the army of Aram.’ So we dwell in Jerusalem.”
Then the word of Yahweh was to Jeremiah, saying,

“Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: ‘Go and say to the man of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, “Will you not receive correction to listen to my words?”—the declaration of Yahweh—

“The words of Jonadab son of Rechab that he commanded his sons, to not drink wine, have been carried out, and they have not drunk until this day, for they have listened to the commandment of their father. But I, I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, but you have not listened to me.

And I have sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying, ‘Turn now, a man from his evil way, and make your deeds good, and do not walk after other gods to serve them, and dwell in the land that I gave to you and to your fathers.’ But you did not incline your ear, and you did not listen to me.
For the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab have carried out the commandment of their father that he commanded them, but this people has not listened to me.”’

Therefore, thus says Yahweh, the God of Armies, the God of Israel: ‘Behold me bringing to Judah and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the disaster that I have spoken against them, because I spoke to them but they did not listen, and I called to them but they did not answer.’”

And to the house of the Rechabites Jeremiah said, “Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: Because you have listened to the commandment of Jonadab your father, and have kept all his commandments, and have done according to all that he commanded you,
therefore thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: ‘A man for Jonadab son of Rechab will not be cut off to stand before my face all the days.’”
Now it happened in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, that this word was to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,

“Take for yourself a scroll of a book, and you shall write on it all the words that I have spoken to you concerning Israel and concerning Judah and concerning all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah and until this day.
Perhaps the house of Judah will listen to all the calamity that I am planning to do to them, so that they may turn back, a man from his evil way, and I will forgive their iniquity and their sin.”
And Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of Yahweh that he had spoken to him on a scroll of a book.
And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, “I am restrained; I am not able to enter the house of Yahweh.

And you, you shall go and shall call out from the scroll what you have written from my mouth, the words of Yahweh, in the ears of the people in the house of Yahweh on the day of fasting. And also in the ears of all Judah, the ones coming from their cities, you shall read them.
Perhaps their supplication will fall to the face of Yahweh, and they will turn back, a man from his evil way; for great is the nose and the heat that Yahweh has spoken against this people.”
And Baruch son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet had commanded him, to read in the book the words of Yahweh in the house of Yahweh.

Now it happened in the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, that all the people in Jerusalem and all the people, the ones coming from the cities of Judah into Jerusalem, proclaimed a fast to the face of Yahweh.

And Baruch called out from the book of the words of Jeremiah in the house of Yahweh, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper courtyard, at the opening of the New Gate of the house of Yahweh, in the ears of all the people.
And Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the words of Yahweh from upon the book.

And he went down to the house of the king, into the chamber of the scribe, and behold, all the officials were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, and Delaiah son of Shemaiah, and Elnathan son of Akbor, and Gemariah son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the officials.
And Micaiah declared to them all the words that he had heard when Baruch read in the book in the ears of the people.

Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi to Baruch, saying, “The scroll that you read from it in the ears of the people—take it in your hand and go.” So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
And they said to him, “Sit, please, and read it in our ears.” And Baruch read in their ears.
And it happened, when they heard all the words, that they expressed dread, a man to his neighbor, and they said to Baruch, “Reporting we must report all these words to the king.”
Then they asked Baruch, saying, “Declare, please, to us: How did you write all these words? From his mouth?”
And Baruch said to them, “From his mouth he called to me all these words, and I was writing upon the book with ink.”
Then the officials said to Baruch, “Go, hide yourself, you and Jeremiah, and let a man not know where you are.”
And they went to the king, into the courtyard, and they deposited the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe. And they reported in the ears of the king all of the words.

Then the king sent Jehudi to take the scroll, and he took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe. And Jehudi read it in the ears of the king and in the ears of all the officials, the ones standing beside the king.
And the king was sitting in the house of the winter, in the ninth month, and the brazier was burning to his face.

And it happened, as Jehudi read three or four columns, that he would cut it up in pieces with the knife of a scribe and throw it into the fire that was on the brazier, until all the scroll was finished on the fire that was on the brazier.
And they were not afraid, and they did not tear their garments—the king and all his servants, the ones hearing all these words.
And even Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah interceded with the king not to burn the scroll, but he did not listen to them.
And the king commanded Jerahmeel son of the king, and Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel, to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet, but Yahweh hid them.
And the word of Yahweh was to Jeremiah after the king burned the scroll, and the words that Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah, saying,
“Return, take for yourself another scroll, and write on it all the former words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say, ‘Thus says Yahweh: “You, you have burned this scroll, saying, ‘Why did you write on it, saying, coming, the king of Babylon will come and destroy this land, and he will cause man and beast to cease from it?’”

Therefore thus says Yahweh concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: ‘There will not be to him one sitting on the throne of David, and his dead body will be thrown to the heat by the day and to the frost by the night.

And I will bring punishment upon him and on his seed and on his servants for their iniquity, and I will bring upon them and upon the dwellers of Jerusalem and to a man of Judah all the calamity that I have spoken to them, but they did not listen.’”

Then Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe, and he wrote on it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book that Jehoiakim king of Judah burned in the fire. And besides these, many words like them were added to them.
And king Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.
But he did not listen, he and his servants and the people of the land, to the words of Yahweh that he spoke by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.
And King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “Pray, please, on behalf of us to Yahweh our God.”
Now Jeremiah was coming and going in the midst of the people, and they had not put him in the house of imprisonment.
And the army of Pharaoh had come out from Egypt, and the Chaldeans, the ones laying siege against Jerusalem, had heard their report and they withdrew from upon Jerusalem.
And the word of Yahweh was to Jeremiah the prophet, saying,

“Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel: Thus you shall say to the king of Judah, the one sending you to me to inquire of me: ‘Behold, the army of Pharaoh, the one coming out to you to help, will return to its own land, Egypt.
And the Chaldeans will return and fight against this city, and they will capture it and burn it with fire.’
Thus says Yahweh: ‘Do not deceive yourselves, saying, “Going, the Chaldeans will go from upon us,” for they will not go.
For even if you had struck all the army of the Chaldeans, the ones fighting with you, and pierced men were left among them, a man in his tent, they would rise up and burn this city with fire.’”
And it happened, when the army of the Chaldeans went up from upon Jerusalem from the face of the army of Pharaoh,
that Jeremiah went out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to divide a share from there in the midst of the people.

And it happened, while he was at the Gate of Benjamin, that a captain of the guard was there, and his name was Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah, and he seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “You are deserting to the Chaldeans!”
And Jeremiah said, “Falsehood! I am not deserting to the Chaldeans.” But he did not listen to him. And Irijah seized Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
And the officials were angry with Jeremiah, and they struck him and put him in the house of bonds, the house of Jonathan the scribe, for they had made it into a house of imprisonment.
So Jeremiah had come to the house of the cistern and to the cells, and Jeremiah stayed there many days.

And King Zedekiah sent and took him out, and the king asked him in his house in secret, and said, “Is there a word from Yahweh?” And Jeremiah said, “There is.” And he said, “Into the hand of the king of Babylon you will be given.”
And Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, “What wrong have I done against you and against your servants and against this people, that you have put me into the house of imprisonment?
And where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, ‘The king of Babylon will not come against you and against this land’?
And now, listen, please, my lord the king. Please let my supplication fall to your face, and may you not make me return to the house of Jonathan the scribe, so I will not die there.

So King Zedekiah commanded, and they committed Jeremiah to the courtyard of the guard, and to give to him a loaf of bread daily from the street of the bakers, until all the bread from the city was finished. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.
And Shephatiah son of Mattan, and Gedaliah son of Pashhur, and Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malkijah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to all the people, saying,

“Thus says Yahweh: The one dwelling in this city will die by the sword, by the famine and by the plague. But the one going out to the Chaldeans will live, and his life will be to him for spoil, and he will live.
Thus says Yahweh: Being given, this city will be given into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.”

And the officials said to the king, “Please let this man be put to death, for on account of this he is weakening the hands of the men of war, the ones remaining in this city, and the hands of all the people by speaking to them according to these words. For this man is not seeking for peace for this people, but rather for harm.”
And King Zedekiah said, “Behold, he is in your hand, for the king is not able to do a word against you.”

And they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malkijah son of the king, which was in the courtyard of the guard, and they let Jeremiah down with ropes. And in the cistern there was no water, but only mud, and Jeremiah sank in the mud.
When Ebed Melech the Cushite, a court official, was in the house of the king, he heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern—and the king was sitting in the Gate of Benjamin—
And Ebed Melech went out from the house of the king and spoke to the king, saying,

“My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they threw into the cistern, and he will die in his place from the face of the hunger, for there is no more bread in the city.”
And the king commanded Ebed Melech the Cushite, saying, “Take in your hand from here 30 men and bring up Jeremiah the prophet from the cistern before he dies.”

And Ebed Melech took the men in his hand and went to the house of the king, to under the storehouse, and he took from there worn-out rags and worn-out clothes and let them down to Jeremiah, into the cistern, with ropes.
And Ebed Melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah, “Please put the worn-out rags and the clothes under your armpits, from under the ropes.” And Jeremiah did so.
And they drew out Jeremiah with the ropes and brought him up from the cistern. And Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.

And King Zedekiah sent and took Jeremiah the prophet to himself, at the third entrance that was in the house of Yahweh. And the king said to Jeremiah, “I am going to ask you a word. May you not hide from me a word.
And Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “If I declare it to you, will you not, putting to death, put me to death? And if I advise you, you will not listen to me.”
Then King Zedekiah swore to Jeremiah in secret, saying, “As Yahweh lives, who made this life for us, I will not put you to death nor give you into the hand of these men who are seeking your life!”

And Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “Thus says Yahweh, the God of Armies, the God of Israel: If, going out, you go out to the officials of the king of Babylon, then your soul will live, and this city will not be burned with fire, and you will live, you and your house.

And if you do not go out to the officials of the king of Babylon, then this city will be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire, and you, you will not escape from their hand.”
And King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “I am fearing the Judeans who have fallen away to the Chaldeans, lest they give me into their hand and they deal ruthlessly with me.”
And Jeremiah said, “They will not give you. Listen, please, to the voice of Yahweh, to what I am speaking to you, that it may go well for you, and your soul may live.
And if you are refusing to go out, this is the word that Yahweh has shown me:

And behold, all the women who are left in the house of the king of Judah are being brought out to the officials of the king of Babylon, and they are saying,
‘They have incited you and have prevailed over you, the men of your peace.
Your feet have been sunk in the mire; they have turned backward.’

And all your wives and your sons they are bringing out to the Chaldeans, and you, you will not escape from their hand, for by the hand of the king of Babylon you will be seized, and this city will burn with fire.”
And Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “Let not a man know about these words, and you will not die.

But if the officials hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say to you, ‘Please declare to us what you spoke to the king and what the king spoke to you; do not hide it from us, and we will not put you to death,’
then you shall say to them, ‘I myself am causing my supplication to fall to the face of the king, so that he would not make me return to the house of Jonathan to die there.’”

Then all the officials came to Jeremiah and asked him, and he declared to them according to all these words that the king had commanded. So they stopped speaking with him, for the matter had not been heard.
And Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard until the day that Jerusalem was captured. And he was there when Jerusalem was captured.
