In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came to Jerusalem, and they besieged against it.
In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city was broken through.

And all the officials of the king of Babylon came and sat in the Middle Gate: Nergal Sarezer, Samgar Nebu, Sarsekim the Rabsaris, Nergal Sarezer the Rabmag, and all the remnant of the officials of the king of Babylon.

And it happened that when Zedekiah king of Judah and all the men of war saw them, then they fled and went out at night from the city, by the way of the garden of the king, through the gate between the two walls. And he went out the way of the Arabah.

But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after them, and they overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. And they took him and brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, to Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he pronounced judgments on him.
And the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah at Riblah before his eyes. And the king of Babylon also slaughtered all the nobles of Judah.
And he put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and he bound him with bronze fetters to bring him to Babylon.
And the Chaldeans burned with fire the house of the king and the house of the people, and the walls of Jerusalem they tore down.

And the rest of the people, the ones remaining in the city, and the ones having fallen away, who had fallen to him, and the rest of the people, the ones remaining, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guards exiled to Babylon.
But from the people, the poor, who there was not to them anything, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guards, left in the land of Judah, and he gave to them vineyards and fields on that day.
And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon commanded concerning Jeremiah by the hand of Nebuzaradan the captain of the guards, saying,
“Take him, and set your eyes on him, and do not do anything harmful to him, but rather, as he speaks to you, thus do with him.”
So Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guards, sent Nebushazban the Rabsaris, and Nergal Sarezer the Rabmag, and all the chiefs of the king of Babylon
and they sent and took Jeremiah from the courtyard of the guard, and they gave him to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan to bring him out to the house. And he dwelt in the midst of the people.
And the word of Yahweh had come to Jeremiah when he was shut up in the courtyard of the guard, saying,

“Go, and you shall say to Ebed Melech the Cushite, saying, ‘Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: Behold me bringing my words against this city for harm and not for good, and they will be to your face on that day.
But I will deliver you on that day’—the declaration of Yahweh—‘and you will not be given into the hand of the men whom you fear from their face.
For rescuing I will rescue you, and by the sword you will not fall, and your life will be to you for spoil, because you have trusted in me’”—the declaration of Yahweh.

The word that was to Jeremiah from Yahweh after Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guards, sent him away from Ramah, when he took him, and he was bound in chains in the midst of all of the exiles of Jerusalem and Judah, the ones being exiled to Babylon.
And the captain of the guards took Jeremiah and said to him, “Yahweh your God spoke this disaster against this place.
And Yahweh brought it and did just as he spoke, because you have sinned against Yahweh and you have not listened to his voice. So this thing has happened to you.

And now, behold, I have loosed you today from the chains that were on your hand. If it is good in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will set my eye on you. But if it is bad in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, refrain. See, all of the land is to your face. Unto the good and to the right in your eyes to go there, go.”

And while he had not yet turned, he said, “So return to Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed in the cities of Judah, and dwell with him in the midst of the people. Or to all the right in your eyes to go, go.” And the captain of the guards gave him an allowance and a gift and sent him away.
Then Jeremiah went to Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, to Mizpah, and he dwelt with him in the midst of the people, the ones having been left in the land.

And all of the captains of the forces who were in the field, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, in the land, and that he had appointed to him men and women and little ones and from the poor of the land, from those who had not been exiled to Babylon.

And they came to Gedaliah, at Mizpah: Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan and Jonathan, the sons of Kareah, and Seraiah, the son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah, the son of the Maacathite, they and their men.

And Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, swore to them and to their men, saying, “Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.

And I, behold me dwelling at Mizpah to stand to the face of the Chaldeans who will come to us. But you, gather wine and summer fruit and oil, and put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have seized.”

And also all of the Jews who were in Moab and among the sons of Ammon and in Edom, and who were in all of the lands, heard that the king of Babylon had given a remnant to Judah, and that he had appointed over them Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan.

And all of the Judeans returned from all of the places where they had been driven there, and they came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah, at Mizpah. And they gathered wine and summer fruit, very much.
And Johanan, the son of Kareah, and all of the captains of the forces who were in the field came to Gedaliah, at Mizpah.

And they said to him, “Knowing, do you know that Baalis, the king of the sons of Ammon, has sent Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, to strike your life?” But Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, did not believe them.

And Johanan, the son of Kareah, said to Gedaliah in secret at Mizpah, saying, “Let me go, please, and I will strike Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, and a man will not know. Why should he strike your life, and all of Judah, the ones being gathered to you, be scattered, and the remnant of Judah perish?”
And Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, said to Johanan, the son of Kareah, “You shall not do this thing, for you are speaking a lie about Ishmael.”

Now it happened in the seventh month, Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, from the seed of the kingdom and the officers of the king, and ten men with him, came to Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, at Mizpah. And they ate bread there together in Mizpah.

And Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, and the ten men who were with him rose up, and they struck Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, with the sword, and he put him to death, whom the king of Babylon had appointed in the land.
And all of the Judeans who were with him, with Gedaliah, in Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who were found there, the men of war, Ishmael struck.
And it happened on the second day after putting Gedaliah to death, and a man did not know it,

and men came from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, eighty men, ones being shaved of beard and torn of clothes and cutting themselves, and a grain offering and frankincense in their hand, to bring them to the house of Yahweh.
And Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, went out to meet them from Mizpah, going to go and weeping. And it happened, as he encountered them, that he said to them, “Come to Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam.”
And it happened, when they came into the midst of the city, that Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, slaughtered them into the midst of the cistern, he and the men who were with him.

But ten men were found among them, and they said to Ishmael, “May you not put us to death, for there is to us stores in the field: wheat and barley and oil and honey.” And he ceased, and he did not put them to death in the midst of their brothers.

And the cistern which Ishmael had thrown there all of the corpses of the men whom he had struck down in the hand of Gedaliah, it that King Asa had made from the face of Baasha, the king of Israel. Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, filled it with the slain.

And Ishmael took captive all of the remnant of the people who were in Mizpah, the daughters of the king and all of the people, the ones having been left in Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guards, had appointed to Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam. And Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, took them captive and went to cross over to the sons of Ammon.
And Johanan, the son of Kareah, and all of the captains of the forces who were with him heard all of the evil that Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, had done,
and they took all of the men and they went to fight with Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah. And they found him at the great pool that is in Gibeon.
And it happened, when all of the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan, the son of Kareah, and all of the captains of the forces who were with him, that they rejoiced.
And all of the people whom Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned around, and they returned and they went to Johanan, the son of Kareah.
But Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, escaped with eight men from the face of Johanan, and he went to the sons of Ammon.

And Johanan, the son of Kareah, and all of the captains of the forces who were with him took all of the remnant of the people whom he had brought back from Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, after he had struck Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam—the mighty men of war, and women and little ones and eunuchs, whom he had brought back from Gibeon.
And they went and stayed in Geruth Kimham, which is beside Bethlehem, to go to enter Egypt,

from the face of the Chaldeans, for they were afraid from their face, because Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, had struck Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed in the land.
Then all the commanders of the forces, and Johanan son of Kareah, and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from small and to great, approached.

And they said to Jeremiah the prophet, “Please, let our supplication fall to your face, and pray for us to Yahweh your God, for all this remnant, because we are left few from many, just as your eyes are seeing us,
that Yahweh your God may declare to us the way in which we should walk and the word that we should do.”

And Jeremiah the prophet said to them, “I have heard. Behold me praying to Yahweh your God according to your words. And it will happen that every word that Yahweh answers you, I will declare to you. I will not withhold a word from you.”
Then they, they said to Jeremiah, “May Yahweh be against us as a witness of truth and being faithful, if not, according to every word with which Yahweh your God sends you to us, thus we do.
Whether good or whether bad, we will listen to the voice of Yahweh our God, to whom we are sending you, in order that it may be good for us when we listen to the voice of Yahweh our God.”
Now it happened at the end of ten days that the word of Yahweh came to Jeremiah.
And he called to Johanan son of Kareah and to all the commanders of the forces who were with him and to all the people, from small and to great.
And he said to them, “Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to make your supplication fall to his face:
‘If turning you will dwell in this land, then I will build you and I will not tear down, and I will plant you and I will not uproot, for I am grieved concerning the disaster that I did to you.

You shall not fear from the face of the king of Babylon, from whose face you are afraid. Do not be afraid of him’—the declaration of Yahweh—‘for I am with you, to save you and to rescue you from his hand.
And I will give to you compassions, that he will have compassion on you and will cause you return to your land.’
But if you are saying, ‘We will not dwell in this land,’ so as not to listen to the voice of Yahweh your God,
saying, ‘No, for we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will not see war and we will not hear the sound of a shofar and we will not hunger for bread, and there we will dwell,’
then now, therefore, hear the word of Yahweh, remnant of Judah. Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: ‘If setting you will set your faces to go to Egypt, and you go to sojourn there,

then it will happen that the sword that you are afraid of, there it will overtake you in the land of Egypt, and the famine that you are anxious about, there it will cling after you to Egypt, and there you will die.

And it will be that all the men who set their faces to go to Egypt to sojourn there will die by the sword, by the famine, and by the plague. And there will not be for them a survivor or a fugitive from the face of the disaster that I am bringing upon them.’

For thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: ‘Just as my nose and my heat were poured out on the dwellers of Jerusalem, so my heat will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. And you will be to execration and to horror and to curse and to taunt, and you will not see this place again.’
Yahweh has spoken concerning you, remnant of Judah: ‘Do not go to Egypt.’ Knowing, you will know that I have given a warning to you today

that you have gone astray at your lives. For you, you sent me to Yahweh your God, saying, ‘Pray on behalf of us to Yahweh our God, and according to all that Yahweh our God says, thus declare it to us, and we will do it.’
And I have declared it to you today, but you have not listened to the voice of Yahweh your God, and to all that he sent me to you.
And now, knowing you will know that by the sword, by the famine, and by the plague you will die in the place where you desire to go to sojourn there.”
And it happened, when Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all the words of Yahweh their God, with which Yahweh their God had sent him to them, all these words,

that Azariah son of Hoshaiah and Johanan son of Kareah and all the arrogant men said, saying to Jeremiah, “Falsehood you are speaking! Yahweh our God did not send you, saying, ‘You shall not go to Egypt to sojourn there.’
For Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you against us, in order to give us into the hand of the Chaldeans, to put us to death or to exile us to Babylon.”
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces and all the people did not listen to the voice of Yahweh, to dwell in the land of Judah.
But Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces took all the remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations where they had been driven there, to sojourn in the land of Judah:

the men and the women and the little ones and the daughters of the king and every soul whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guards had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
And they came to the land of Egypt, for they did not listen to the voice of Yahweh. And they came as far as Tahpanhes.
And the word of Yahweh was to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
“Take in your hand large stones, and you shall hide them in the mortar in the brick pavement that is at the entrance of the house of Pharaoh in Tahpanhes, before the eyes of the Judean men.

And you shall say to them, ‘Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: “Behold me, sending, and I will take Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I will set his throne above these stones that I have hidden, and he will spread out his canopy over them.
And he will come and he will strike the land of Egypt: whoever is for death, to death; and whoever is for captivity, to captivity; and whoever is for the sword, to the sword.

And I will kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and he will take them captive. And he will wrap himself with the land of Egypt just as the shepherd wraps himself with his garment, and he will go out from there in peace.
And he will break the pillars of Beth Shemesh that are in the land of Egypt, and the houses of the gods of Egypt he will burn with fire.”’”
The word that came to Jeremiah for all the Jews, the ones dwelling in the land of Egypt, the ones dwelling in Migdol and in Tahpanhes and in Memphis and in the land of Pathros, saying,

“Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: ‘You yourself have seen all the disaster that I have brought upon Jerusalem and upon all the cities of Judah. And behold them, a ruin this day, and there is no dweller in them,
from the face of their evil that they did to provoke me to anger, by going to burn incense, to serve other gods that they did not know—they, you, nor your fathers.
And I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending, saying, “Please, do not do this thing of abomination that I hate.”
But they did not listen and they did not incline their ear to turn back from their evil, so as not to burn incense to other gods.
And my heat and my nose poured out, and it burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, and they became a ruin, a desolation, as at this day.’

And now, thus says Yahweh, the God of Armies, the God of Israel: ‘Why are you doing great evil against your souls, to cut yourselves off, man and woman, child and nursing one, from the midst of Judah, so as not to leave for yourselves a remnant,

by provoking me to anger with the works of your hands, by burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you are going to sojourn there, in order to cut yourselves off and in order for you to become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?

Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers and the evils of the kings of Judah and the evils of his wives and your evils and the evils of your wives that they did in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
They have not been crushed to this day, and they have not feared, and they have not walked in my law and in my statutes that I gave to the face of you and to the face of your fathers.’
Therefore thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel: ‘Behold me, setting my face against you for disaster, and to cut off all Judah.

And I will take the remnant of Judah who set their faces to go to the land of Egypt to sojourn there, and they will all come to an end in the land of Egypt. They will fall by the sword; by the famine they will come to an end, from small and to great. By the sword and by the famine they will die, and they will be to execration, to horror, and to curse, and to taunt.
And I will visit upon the ones dwelling in the land of Egypt just as I visited upon Jerusalem, by the sword, by the famine, and by the plague.

So there will not be a fugitive or a survivor for the remnant of Judah, the ones going to sojourn there in the land of Egypt, or to return to the land of Judah, where they are lifting up their soul to return to dwell there. For they will not return, except fugitives.’”

And all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, and all the women standing by, a great assembly, and all the people dwelling in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying,
“The word that you have spoken to us in the name of Yahweh—we are not listening to you.

For doing we will do every word that has gone out from our mouth, to burn incense to the queen of the heavens and to pour out drink offerings to her, as we have done, we and our fathers, our kings and our officials, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. And we were satisfied with bread and we had good, and disaster we did not see.
But from when we ceased to burn incense to the queen of the heavens and to pour out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything, and by the sword and by the famine we have come to an end.

And when we were burning incense to the queen of the heavens and poured out drink offerings to her, was it without our husbands that we made for her cakes to copy her and pour out to her drink offerings?”
And Jeremiah said to all the people, to the men, and to the women, and to all the people answering him that word, saying,

“As for the incense that you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem—you and your fathers, your kings and your officials and the people of the land—has Yahweh not remembered them, and it come to his heart?

And Yahweh was no longer able to bear it, from the face of the evil of your deeds, from the face of the abominations that you did. And your land became a ruin and a horror and a curse, without a dweller, as at this day.

From the face of the fact that you have burned incense and that you have sinned against Yahweh, and you have not listened to the voice of Yahweh, and in his law and in his statutes and in his testimonies you have not walked—therefore this disaster has met you, as at this day.”
And Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women, “Hear the word of Yahweh, all Judah who are in the land of Egypt.

Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, saying: ‘You and your wives have spoken with your mouth and you have fulfilled it with your hands, saying, “Performing we will perform our vows that we vowed, to burn incense to the queen of the heavens and to pour out drink offerings to her.” Establishing you will establish your vows, and performing you will perform your vows!’

Therefore hear the word of Yahweh, all Judah, the ones dwelling in the land of Egypt: ‘Behold me, I have sworn by my great name,’ says Yahweh, ‘My name will no longer be called by the mouth of any man of Judah, saying, “By the life of Lord Yahweh,” in all the land of Egypt.
Behold me, watching over them for harm and not for good. And all the men of Judah who are in the land of Egypt will come to an end by the sword and by the famine, until their finishing.

And the fugitives of the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, men of number. And all the remnant of Judah, the ones coming to the land of Egypt to sojourn there, will know whose word will stand, from me or from them.
And this will be for you a sign’—the declaration of Yahweh—‘that I am visiting punishment upon you in this place, so that you may know that standing my words will stand against you for harm.’

Thus says Yahweh: ‘Behold me, giving Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of the ones seeking his life, just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy and the one seeking his life.’”
The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah, when he wrote these words on a book from the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying,
“Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel, concerning you, Baruch:
You have said, ‘Woe now to me, for Yahweh has added sorrow to my pain. I am weary with my groaning, and I have not rest found!’
Thus you shall say to him: ‘Thus says Yahweh: Behold, what I have built, I am tearing down, and what I have planted, I am plucking up—and this with regard to all of the earth.

And you, do you seek great things for yourself? May you not seek them. For behold me, bringing disaster upon all flesh’—the declaration of Yahweh—‘but I will give to you your life for spoil in all the places where you will go there.’”
The word of Yahweh that was to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.

For Egypt: concerning the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was at the river Euphrates in Carchemish, and which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:

“Arrange small shield and large shield,
and draw near for the battle.

Harness the horses, and go up, O horsemen,
and station yourselves with helmets.
Polish the spears, put on the body armor.

Why have I seen it? They are dismayed, turning back backward,
and their mighty ones are crushed.
And in flight they have fled, and they have not turned.
Terror from all around”—the declaration of Yahweh—

“The swift cannot flee, and the mighty one cannot escape.
In the north, by the side of the Euphrates River, they stumble and they fall.

Who is this rising up like the Nile,
like the streams their surging back and forth its waters?

Egypt rises up like the Nile, and like the streams its waters toss.
And he said, ‘Let me rise, let me cover the earth. Let me destroy city and the dwellers in it.’

Go up, O horses, and drive madly O chariots, and let the mighty ones come out,
Cush and Put, the ones grasping the shield, and men of Lud, ones grasping, ones treading the bow.

And that day is to Lord Yahweh of Armies, a day of vengeance, to avenge himself on his adversaries.
And the sword will devour and be satisfied and be quenched from their blood,
for there is a sacrifice for Lord Yahweh of Armies in the land of the north, by the Euphrates River.
The word that Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, regarding the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:

“Declare it in Egypt, and cause it to be heard in Migdol, and cause it to be heard in Memphis and in Tahpanhes.
Say, ‘Station yourself and prepare yourself,
for a sword will devour those around you.’

Why have your mighty ones been cut down? They did not stand,
because Yahweh has thrust them down.

He multiplied the one stumbling; yes, a man has fallen upon his neighbor.
And they said, ‘Arise, and let us return to our people and to the land of our birth,
from the face of the sword of the oppressor.’

There they call out,
‘Pharaoh king of Egypt is a loud noise; he has let the appointed time to pass by.’

As I live”—the declaration of the King, Yahweh of Armies is his name—“surely like Tabor among the mountains,
and like Carmel by the sea, he will come.

Prepare baggage for yourself for exile, O dweller, daughter of Egypt,
for Memphis will become a desolation, and it will be burned, without a dweller.

Egypt is a beautiful, beautiful heifer;
a gadfly from the north coming, coming.

Her sound is like a serpent that goes away,
for in force they go, and with axes they have come against her, like men cutting down trees.

They have cut down her forest”—the declaration of Yahweh—“for it will not be searched out,
for they are more numerous than the locust, and there is no number to them.

The daughter of Egypt will be put to shame;
she will be given into the hand of the people of the north.”

Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says, “Behold me, visiting punishment upon Amon from No, and upon Pharaoh, and upon Egypt, and upon her gods, and upon her kings, and upon Pharaoh, and upon the ones trusting in him.

And I will give them into the hand of the ones seeking their life, and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of his servants. And after that she will dwell as in the days of antiquity”—the declaration of Yahweh.

“But you, do not fear, my servant Jacob, nor be dismayed, Israel, for behold me, saving you from far off, and your seed from the land of their captivity. And Jacob will return and will have quiet and will be at ease, and there will be no one making him afraid.

You, my servant Jacob, do not fear”—the declaration of Yahweh— “for I am with you. For I will make a complete end of all the nations where I have scattered you there, but you I will not make a complete end of. And I will discipline you according to justice, and leaving unpunished, I will not leave you unpunished.”
The word of Yahweh that was to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.

Thus says Yahweh:
“Behold, waters are rising from the north,
and they will become as an overflowing torrent.
And they will overflow the land and its fullness,
the city and the dwellers in it.
And mankind will cry out,
and every dweller of the land will wail.

At the sound of the stamping of the hooves of his mighty ones,
at the rattling of his chariot, the rumble of his wheels,
fathers do not turn to sons
from the slackness of hands,

because of the day that is coming
to devastate all the Philistines,
to cut off from Tyre and from Sidon every remaining one helping.
For Yahweh is devastating the Philistines,
the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor.

Baldness has come to Gaza;
Ashkelon has been destroyed,
O remnant of their valley,
until when will you cut yourself?

‘Ah, sword of Yahweh!
How long will you not be quiet?
Be gathered into your sheath;
be at rest and be still.’

How can it be quiet,
when Yahweh has given a command to it?
Against Ashkelon and against the coast of the sea,
there he has appointed it.”

Concerning Moab: Thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel:
“Woe to Nebo, for she is devastated!
Kiriathaim is ashamed; she is captured.
The stronghold is put to shame and is dismayed.

There is no longer praise of Moab.
In Heshbon they have devised evil against her:
‘Come, and let us cut her off from being a nation.’
Also, O Madmen, you will be silenced;
after you the sword will go.

A sound of a cry from Horonaim:
destruction and great breaking!

Moab is broken;
her little ones have a cry heard.

For the ascent of Luhith—
with weeping he goes up weeping;
for at the descent of Horonaim
the adversaries have heard a cry of breaking.

Flee! Save yourselves,
and you will be like a juniper bush in the wilderness.

For because of your trusting in your works and in your treasures,
you also will be captured.
And Chemosh will go out into exile,
his priests and his officials together.

And a destroyer will come to every city,
and no city will escape.
And the valley will perish and the plateau will be destroyed,
as Yahweh has said.

Give wing to Moab, for to fly she will go away,
and her cities will become a desolation,
with no dweller in them.

Cursed is the one doing the work of Yahweh with slackness,
and cursed is the one withholding his sword from blood.

Moab has been at ease from his youth,
and he is undisturbed on his dregs.
And he has not been emptied from vessel to vessel,
and into exile he has not gone.
Therefore his taste stands in him,
and his scent has not changed.
Therefore, behold, days are coming”—the declaration of Yahweh—“when I will send to him tippers, and they will tip him. And they will empty his vessels and they will shatter their jars.

And Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh,
just as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, their confidence.

How can you say, ‘We are mighty,
and men of valor for battle’?

Moab is devastated, and he has gone up against her cities;
and the choicest of his young men have gone down to the slaughter, the declaration of the King, Yahweh of Armies is his name.

The calamity of Moab is near to coming,
and his disaster hastens exceedingly.

Grieve for him, all of you around him,
and all the knowers of his name.
Say, ‘How the staff of strength is broken,
the rod of splendor!’

Come down from glory and sit in thirst,
dweller, daughter of Dibon,
for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you;
he has ruined your fortifications.

Stand by the road and watch,
dweller of Aroer.
Ask him fleeing and her escaping;
say, ‘What has happened?’

Moab is put to shame, for she is dismayed.
Wail and cry out!
Declare it by Arnon
that Moab is devastated.

And judgment has come to the land of the plateau,
to Holon and to Jahaz and upon Mephaath,
and upon Dibon and upon Nebo and upon Beth Diblathaim,
and upon Kiriathaim and upon Beth Gamul and upon Beth Meon,

and upon Kerioth and upon Bozrah,
and upon all the cities of the land of Moab,
the far and the near.

The horn of Moab has been cut off,
and his arm has been broken”—the declaration of Yahweh.
“Make him drunk, because against Yahweh he has made himself great. And Moab will splash in his vomit, and he will be for derision, also he.
For did not Israel come to be a derision to you? Was he found among thieves, that as often as your words were about him you shook?

Abandon the cities and dwell among the rock,
dwellers of Moab,
and be like a dove that nests
in the sides of the mouth of a pit.

We have heard of the pride of Moab—exceedingly proud—
his loftiness and his pride and his arrogance and the height of his heart.

I, I know”—the declaration of Yahweh—“his outburst, but his boasts are not trustworthy;
his deeds are not trustworthy.

More than the weeping of Jazer I will weep for you,
vine of Sibmah.
Your tendrils passed over to the sea;
as far as the sea of Jazer they reached.
Upon your summer fruit and upon your grape harvest
a destroyer has fallen.

And gladness and rejoicing have been taken away
from the fertile land and from the land of Moab.
And I have caused wine to cease from the winepresses.
He will not tread with a shout;
the shout will not be a shout.
From the outcry of Heshbon as far as Elealeh, as far as Jahaz, they have given their voice, from Zoar as far as Horonaim, Eglath Shelishiyah, for even the waters of Nimrim will become desolations.
And I will cause to cease for Moab”—the declaration of Yahweh—“the one causing offerings to ascend on a high place and the one burning incense to his gods.
Therefore my heart moans for Moab like flutes, and my heart moans like flutes for the men of Kir Hareseth. Therefore the abundance he has acquired has perished.
For every head will be baldness, and every beard will be clipped On all hands will be gashes, and on the loins will be sackcloth.
On all the housetops of Moab and in her open squares, all of it lamentation, for I have broken Moab like a vessel without delight in it”—the declaration of Yahweh.

“How it is dismayed! They wail!
How Moab has turned the neck in shame!
Moab has come to be for a derision
and a terror to all around him.”

For thus says Yahweh:
“Behold, like an eagle he will swoop down,
and he will spread his wings against Moab.

Kerioth has been captured,
and the strongholds have been seized.
And the heart of the warriors of Moab in that day
will be like the heart of a woman in labor.

And Moab will be destroyed from being a people,
for against Yahweh he has made himself great.
Terror and pit and snare are upon you, dweller of Moab”—the declaration of Yahweh.

“The one fleeing from the face of the terror will fall into the pit,
and the one coming up from the pit will be caught in the snare,
for I will bring to her, to Moab,
the year of their visitation”—the declaration of Yahweh.

“In the shadow of Heshbon the ones fleeing stand without strength,
for a fire has gone forth from Heshbon,
and a flame from the midst of Sihon,
and it has devoured the forehead of Moab
and the crown of the head of the sons of tumult.

Woe to you, Moab!
The people of Chemosh have perished,
for your sons have been taken into captivity,
and your daughters into captivity.

Yet I will restore the restoration of Moab in the end of the days”—the declaration of Yahweh.
As far as here is the judgment of Moab.

Concerning the sons of Ammon, thus says Yahweh:
“Are there no sons for Israel?
Or is there no heir for him?
Why then has their king taken possession of Gad,
and his people dwelt in his cities?

Therefore, behold, days are coming”—the declaration of Yahweh—
“when I will make the shout of war heard against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon,
and she will become a mound of desolation,
and her daughters will be kindled with fire.
And Israel will take possession of his possessors,”
says Yahweh.

“Wail, Heshbon, for Ai has been devastated!
Cry out, daughters of Rabbah!
Put on sackcloth; mourn,
and run to and fro among the walls,
for their king will go into exile,
his priests and his officials together.

Why do you boast in the valleys,
your valley flowing, apostate daughter,
the one trusting in her treasures,
‘Who will come against me?’

Behold me, bringing terror upon you”—the declaration of the Lord Yahweh of Armies—
“from all of those around you.
And you will be scattered, a man to his face,
and there will be no one gathering the one fleeing.
But after that I will restore the restoration of the sons of Ammon”—the declaration of Yahweh.

Concerning Edom, thus says Yahweh of Armies:
“Is there no longer wisdom in Teman?
Counsel has perished from the discerning ones;
their wisdom has rotted away.

Flee! Turn back! Make deep to dwell,
dwellers of Dedan!
For I will bring the calamity of Esau upon him,
the time I visit him.

If grape gatherers came to you,
would they not leave gleanings?
If thieves came in the night,
they would destroy their sufficiency.

But I, I will strip Esau bare;
I will uncover his hiding places,
and he will not be able to hide himself.
His seed is devastated, and his brothers and his neighbors,
and he is no more.

Leave your fatherless ones; I, I will keep them alive,
and let your widows trust in me.”

For thus says Yahweh: “Behold, those whose judgment was not to drink the cup, drinking they will drink. And you, are you the one who, acquitting, will be acquitted? You will not be acquitted, but drinking you will drink.
For by myself I have sworn”—the declaration of Yahweh— “that Bozrah will become a horror, a reproach, a desolation, and for a curse, and all of her cities will become ruins of perpetuity.”

I have heard a report from Yahweh,
and an envoy has been sent among the nations:
“Gather yourselves and come against her,
and rise up for the battle!”

“For behold, I will make you small among the nations,
despised among mankind.

Your terror has deceived you,
the pride of your heart,
one dwelling in the clefts of the rock,
grasping the height of the hill.
Though you make your nest high like the eagle,
from there I will bring you down”—the declaration of Yahweh.

“And Edom will become a horror.
Everyone passing by her will be appalled
and will hiss over all of her wounds.

“Like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and her neighbors,” says Yahweh,
“no man will dwell there,
and a son of man will not sojourn in her.

Behold, like a lion he will come up from the thicket of the Jordan
against the pastureland of continual.
For I will act in a moment, I will make him run away from her.
And who is the chosen one whom I will appoint over her?
For who is like me, and who will summon me?
And who is this shepherd who will stand before my face?”

Therefore hear the counsel of Yahweh
that he has planned against Edom,
and his purposes that he has devised
against the dwellers of Teman:
Surely they will drag away the little ones of the flock!
Surely their own pasture will be appalled over them!
From the sound of their falling the earth will quake. A cry—at the Sea of Reeds her voice was heard.

Behold, like an eagle he will come up and swoop,
and he will spread his wings over Bozrah.
And the heart of the warriors of Edom on that day
will be like the heart of a woman in labor.”

Concerning Damascus:
“Hamath and Arpad are ashamed,
for they have heard a bad report.
They melt;there is anxiety by the sea—
it is not able to keep quiet.

Damascus has become feeble;
she has turned to flee, and trembling has seized her.
Distress and pangs have seized her
like a woman giving birth.

How is the city of praise not forsaken,
the city of my joy?

“Therefore her young men will fall in her open squares,
and all the men of war will be silenced in that day”—the declaration of Yahweh of Armies.

“And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus,
and it will devour the palaces of Ben Hadad.”

Concerning Kedar and concerning the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck, thus says Yahweh:
“Arise, go up against Kedar,
and destroy the sons of the east!

They will take their tents and their flocks;
they will carry off for themselves their curtains and all of their vessels and their camels.
And they will cry out over them,
‘Terror from all around!’

Flee! Wander far away! Make deep to dwell, dwellers of Hazor”—the declaration of Yahweh—
“for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has counseled a counsel against you,
and he has planned a plan against them.

And their camels will become plunder,
and the multitude of their livestock spoil.
And I will scatter them to every wind,
the ones cutting at the corner,
and from all of his sides I will bring their calamity”—the declaration of Yahweh.

And Hazor will become a habitation of jackals,
a desolation unto eternity.
No man will dwell there,
and a son of man will not sojourn in her.
The word of Yahweh that was to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying,

Thus says Yahweh of Armies:
“Behold me, breaking the bow of Elam,
the chief source of their power.

And I will bring against Elam the four winds
from the four ends of the heavens,
and I will scatter them to all of these winds,
and there will not be a nation
where the banished ones of Elam will not go there.

And I will make Elam dismayed before the face of their enemies
and before the face of the ones seeking their life.
And I will bring disaster upon them, the burning of my nose”—the declaration of Yahweh—
“and I will send the sword after them until I have finished them.

And I will set my throne in Elam,
and I will destroy from there king and officials”—the declaration of Yahweh.
“Yet it will happen in the end of the days that I will restore the restoration of Elam”—the declaration of Yahweh.
The word that Yahweh spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet,

“Declare among the nations and cause it to be heard,
and lift up a banner; cause it to be heard!
May you not conceal it!
Say, ‘Babylon has been captured;
Bel has come to shame; Marduk is dismayed.
Her idols have come to shame;
her images are dismayed.’

For a nation will come up against her from the north.
It, it will set her land as a horror,
and there will not be a dweller in her.
From man even to beast, they will wander; they will go out.

In those days and in that time”—the declaration of Yahweh—
“the sons of Israel will come, they and the sons of Judah together.
Going and weeping they will go,
and they will seek Yahweh their God.

They will ask the way to Zion;
their faces are facing this way.
‘Come!’ And they will join themselves to Yahweh
in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.

All of their finders have devoured them,
and their adversaries have said, ‘We are not guilty,
because they have sinned against Yahweh, the pasture of righteousness
and the hope of their fathers—Yahweh.’

And Chaldea will become plunder;
all of her plunderers will be satisfied”—the declaration of Yahweh.

“Though you rejoice, though you exult,
plunderers of my inheritance;
though you leap about like a heifer threshing,
and you neigh like mighty ones,

your mother is greatly ashamed;
the one bearing you is humiliated.
Behold, the last of nations
is a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.

From the wrath of Yahweh she will not be inhabited,
and she will become a desolation, all of her.
Everyone passing by Babylon will be appalled
and will hiss over all of her wounds.

Array yourselves against Babylon all around,
all of the ones bending a bow!
Shoot at her; may you not spare an arrow,
for she has sinned against Yahweh.

Cut off the sower from Babylon,
and the one grasping the sickle at the time of harvest.
From the face of the oppressing sword
each man will turn to his people, and each man will flee to his land.

Israel is a scattered sheep; lions have driven him away.
The first one, the king of Assyria, devoured him,
and this last one, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon,
has broken his bones.”
Therefore thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, “Behold me, visiting punishment upon the king of Babylon and upon his land, just as I visited punishment upon the king of Assyria.

And I will bring Israel back to his pasture,
and he will graze on Carmel and Bashan;
and in the hill country of Ephraim and Gilead
his soul will be satisfied.

In those days and in that time”—the declaration of Yahweh—
“the iniquity of Israel will be sought, and there will be none,
and the sins of Judah, and they will not be found;
for I will forgive the ones whom I leave remaining.

Concerning the land of Merathaim: go up against her,
and against the dwellers of Pekod.
Destroy and devote them to destruction after them”—the declaration of Yahweh—
“and do according to all that I have commanded you.

A sound of battle is in the land,
and a great breaking.

How the hammer of all the earth
has been cut down and broken!
How Babylon has become a horror
among the nations!

I laid a snare for you, and you were also captured, Babylon,
and you, you did not know.
You were found and also seized,
for you have contended against Yahweh.

Yahweh has opened his storehouse
and has brought out the weapons of his indignation,
for it is a work for my Lord Yahweh of Armies
in the land of the Chaldeans.

Destroy all of her bulls; they will go down to the slaughter.
Woe to them, for their day has come,
the time of their visitation.

A sound of the fugitives and of survivors from the land of Babylon,
to declare in Zion
the vengeance of Yahweh our God, the vengeance of his temple.

Summon archers against Babylon!
All of the ones bending a bow, encamp against her all around.
May there not be an escape for her.
Repay her according to her deed;
according to all that she has done, do to her.
For she has acted presumptuously against Yahweh,
against the Holy One of Israel.

Therefore her young men will fall in her open squares,
and all of the men of her war will be silenced in that day”—the declaration of Yahweh.

“Behold me against you, presumption”—the declaration of the Lord Yahweh of Armies—
“for your day has come,
the time when I visit punishment upon you.

And presumption will stumble and fall,
and there will be no one raising him up.
And I will kindle a fire in his cities,
and it will devour all of those around him.”

Thus says Yahweh of Armies,
“The sons of Israel are oppressed, and the sons of Judah together,
and all of their captors have held them fast;
they have refused to send them away.

Their Redeemer is strong; Yahweh of Armies is his name.
Contending he will contend their dispute,
in order to make the land be at rest
and to make the dwellers of Babylon tremble.

A sword is against the Chaldeans”—the declaration of Yahweh—
“and against the dwellers of Babylon,
and against her officials and against her wise ones.

A sword is against the liars, and they will become fools.
A sword is against her warriors, and they will be dismayed.

A sword is against his horses and against his chariot,
and against all of the mixed company that is in her midst,
and they will become like women.
A sword is against her storehouses, and they will be plundered.

A drought is against her waters, and they will dry up.
For it is a land of carved images,
and by the terrors they act madly.

Therefore desert beasts will dwell with hyenas,
and daughters of ostriches will dwell in her.
And she will not be inhabited again forever,
and she will not be dwelt in unto generation and generation.

Like God overthrowing Sodom and Gomorrah and her neighbors”—the declaration of Yahweh—
“no man will dwell there,
and a son of man will not sojourn in her.

Behold, a people is coming from the north,
and a great nation and many kings
are being stirred up from the remote parts of the earth.

They grasp bow and curved sword;
they are cruel and will not have compassion.
Their voice roars like the sea,
and they ride on horses,
arrayed like a man for the battle
against you, daughter of Babylon.

The king of Babylon has heard their report,
and his hands have become feeble.
Distress has seized him,
anguish like a woman giving birth.

Behold, like a lion he will come up from the pride of the Jordan
to a pasture of a permanent stream,
so in a moment I will make them run from her.
And who is the chosen one whom I will appoint over her?
For who is like me, and who will summon me?
And who is this shepherd who will stand before my face?”

Therefore hear the counsel of Yahweh
that he has counseled against Babylon,
and his plans that he has planned
against the land of the Chaldeans:
If they do not drag them away, the little ones of the flock!
If he does not make their pasture desolate over them!

From the sound of Babylon being seized the earth has quaked,
and an outcry among the nations has been heard.

Thus says Yahweh:
“Behold me, arousing against Babylon
and against the dwellers of Leb Kamai
a destroying wind.

And I will send strangers to Babylon,
and they will winnow her and will empty her land,
for they will be against her from all around
in the day of evil.

Against let him tread, let him tread, the one treading his bow,
and against let him rise up in his body armor,
but do not have pity on her young men;
devote all of her army to destruction.

And the slain will fall in the land of the Chaldeans,
and the pierced ones in her streets.”

For Israel is not widowed, nor Judah, from his God,
from Yahweh of Armies,
though their land is full of guilt
from the Holy One of Israel.

Flee from the midst of Babylon,
and each of you save his life!
Do not be destroyed in her iniquity,
for the time of vengeance it is for Yahweh;
it isa recompense he is repaying to her.

Babylon was a cup of gold in the hand of Yahweh,
making all the earth drunk.
From her wine the nations drank;
therefore the nations are acting madly.

Suddenly Babylon has fallen and has been broken.
Wail over her!
Take balm for her pain;
perhaps she will be healed.

“We healed Babylon, but she was not healed.
Abandon her, and let us go, each man to his land,
for her judgment has reached to the heavens
and has been lifted up to the clouds.

Yahweh has brought out our righteousnesses.
Come, and let us recount in Zion the work of Yahweh our God.”

Sharpen the arrows! Fill the quivers!
Yahweh has aroused the spirit of the kings of Media,
for his plan against Babylon is to destroy her,
for it is
the vengeance of Yahweh, the vengeance of his temple.

Against the walls of Babylon lift up a banner!
Strengthen the watch! Raise up watchers!
Prepare the ambushers!
For Yahweh has both planned and also done
what he spoke against the dwellers of Babylon.

Dweller upon many waters, abundant in treasures,
your end has come, the cubit of your severing.

Yahweh of Armies has sworn by his life:
“Surely I will fill you with mankind like the locust,
and they will raise a shout over you.”

The maker of the earth by his power,
the establisher of the world by his wisdom—
and by his understanding he stretched out the heavens.

At the sound of his giving, there is a tumult of waters in the heavens,
and he makes clouds go up from the end of the earth.
He makes lightnings for the rain,
and he brings out wind from his storehouses.

Every man is stupid, without knowledge.
Every metalworker has come to shame from a carved image,
for his cast image is a lie,
and there is no breath in them.

They are vapor, a work of mockeries.
In the time of their visitation they will perish.

Not like these is the portion of Jacob,
for he is the one forming all things,
and the tribe of his inheritance.
Yahweh of Armies is his name.

“You are a shatterer for me, weapons of war,
and with you I have shattered nations,
and with you I have destroyed kingdoms.

And with you I have shattered horse and his rider,
and with you I have shattered chariot and his rider.

And with you I have shattered man and woman,
and with you I have shattered old man and youth,
and with you I have shattered young man and virgin.

And with you I have shattered shepherd and his flock,
and with you I have shattered plowman and his team,
and with you I have shattered governors and prefects.
And I will repay to Babylon and to all the dwellers of Chaldea all their evil that they did in Zion to your eyes”—the declaration of Yahweh.

“Behold me, against you, mountain of destruction”—the declaration of Yahweh—“the one destroying all the earth.
And I will stretch out my hand against you,
and I will roll you from the cliffs,
and I will make you into a mountain of burning.

And they will not take from you a stone for a corner
or a stone for foundations,
for you will be desolations of perpetuity”—the declaration of Yahweh.

Lift up a banner in the land!
Blow a shofar among the nations!
Consecrate nations against her!
Make the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz hear the call against her!
Appoint a marshal against her!
Bring up horses like the bristling locust!

Consecrate nations against her:
the kings of Media, her governors and all her prefects,
and all the land of his dominion.

And the land quaked and writhed,
for the plans of Yahweh have stood against Babylon,
to make the land of Babylon a desolation,
without a dweller.

The warriors of Babylon have ceased to fight;
they have remained in the strongholds.
Their might has dried up; they have become as women.
They have set her dwellings on fire; her bars have been broken.

A runner runs to meet a runner,
and an announcer to meet an announcer,
to announce to the king of Babylon
that his city has been captured from its end,

and the fords have been seized,
and the marshes they have burned with fire,
and the men of war are terrified.

For thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel:
“Daughter Babylon is like a threshing floor
at the time of treading her.
Yet a little while,
and the time of the harvest will come for her.”

“My violence and my flesh be upon Babylon,”
the dweller of Zion says.
“And my blood be upon the dwellers of Chaldea,”
says Jerusalem.

Therefore thus says Yahweh:
“Behold me, contending your contention,
and I will avenge your vengeance,
and I will dry up her sea,
and I will make her fountain dry.

And Babylon will become heaps,
a habitation of jackals,
a desolation and a hissing, without a dweller.

Together like the young lions they roar;
they growl like the cubs of lions.

When they grow hot, I will set out their feast,
and I will make them drunk, so that they may exult
and sleep a sleep of perpetuity
and not wake up”—the declaration of Yahweh.

“I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter,
like rams with male goats.”

How Sheshach has been captured,
and the praise of all the earth has been seized!
How Babylon has become a desolation
among the nations!

The sea has come up over Babylon;
she has been covered with the tumult of its waves.

Her cities have become a desolation,
a land of dryness and a desert plain,
a land no man dwells in them,
and a son of man does not pass through them.

“And I will visit upon Bel in Babylon,
and I will bring out his swallowing from his mouth,
and the nations will not stream to him anymore.
Even the wall of Babylon has fallen.

Go out from her midst, my people,
and each of you save his life
from the burning of the nose of Yahweh!

And lest your heart grow soft
and you fear at the report that is heard in the land—
and the report will come in the one year,
and after it in the next year the report,
and violence in the land,
and ruler against ruler.

Therefore, behold, days are coming
and I will visit upon the carved images of Babylon,
and all of her land will be put to shame,
and all of her slain will fall in her midst.

And the heavens and the earth and all that is in them
will shout for joy over Babylon,
for from the north the destroyers will come to her”—the declaration of Yahweh.

Also Babylon is to fall for the slain of Israel,
as also for Babylon the slain of all the earth have fallen.

Fugitives from the sword, go! Do not stand still!
Remember Yahweh from afar,
and may Jerusalem come up on your heart.

“We are ashamed, for we have heard a reproach;
disgrace has covered our faces,
for strangers have entered
upon the holy places of the house of Yahweh.”

“Therefore, behold, days are coming”—the declaration of Yahweh—“and I will visit upon her carved images,
and in all her land the slain will groan.

Though Babylon should go up to the heavens,
and though she should fortify the height of her strength,
from me destroyers would come to her”—the declaration of Yahweh.

A sound of an outcry from Babylon,
and a great breaking from the land of the Chaldeans!

For Yahweh is devastating Babylon,
and he will destroy from her the great voice.
And their waves will roar like many waters;
the roaring of their voice is given.

“And I will make her officials and her wise men,
her governors and her prefects and her warriors drunk,
and they will sleep a sleep of perpetuity
and not wake up”—the declaration of the King; Yahweh of Armies is his name.

Thus says Yahweh of Armies:
“The broad walls of Babylon—stripping bare, it will be stripped bare,
and her high gates will burn with fire.
And the peoples will labor for emptiness,
and the communities for fire,
and they will grow weary.”

The word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Now Seraiah was the officer of the resting place.
And Jeremiah wrote all of the evil that would come to Babylon in one scroll, all of these words that were written concerning Babylon.
And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you come to Babylon, then you shall see and you shall read aloud all of these words,
then you shall say, ‘Yahweh, you, you have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, to not be in it a dweller, to from man and to beast, for it shall be desolations of perpetuity.’
And it shall be, when you have finished reading this scroll aloud, you shall tie a stone to it and throw it into the midst of the Euphrates,
and you shall say, ‘Thus Babylon will sink and will not rise, from the face of the evil that I am bringing upon her, and they will grow weary.’” Until here are the words of Jeremiah.
Zedekiah was a son of 21 years when he reigned, and he reigned 11 years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
And he did evil in the eyes of Yahweh, like all that Jehoiakim had done.
For because of the nose of Yahweh it was against Jerusalem and Judah, until he cast them away from his face. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

And it happened in the ninth year of his reigning, in the tenth month, on ten of the month, Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, came, he and all of his army, against Jerusalem. And he encamped against it, and they built a siege mound against it all around.
And the city entered into siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
In the fourth month, on nine of the month, then famine seized the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

And the city was breached, and all of the men of war fled and went out from the city at night the way of the gate between the two walls that were near the garden of the king (now the Chaldeans were against the city all around), and they went the way of the Arabah.
But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and they overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. And all of his army were scattered away from him.
And they captured the king, and they brought him up to the king of Babylon, to Riblah in the land of Hamath. And they pronounced judgment on him.
And the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah to his eyes, and he also slaughtered all of the leaders of Judah at Riblah.
And he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah, and he bound him with two bronze chains, and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon, and he put him in a house of oversight until the day of his death.

And in the fifth month, on seven of the month, it was the year of 19, the year to King Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, the chief of the guards, he stood to the face of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
And he burned the house of Yahweh and the house of the king. And all of the houses of Jerusalem and every house of the great, he burned with fire.
And all of the walls of Jerusalem all around, all of the army of the Chaldeans who were with the chief of the guards tore down.

And the poor of the people and the rest of the people left in the city and the ones having fallen, who had fallen to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude, Nebuzaradan, the chief of the guards, exiled.
But Nebuzaradan, the chief of the guards, let some of the poor of the land remain as vinedressers and as farmers.

And the Chaldeans broke up the pillars of bronze that were to the house of Yahweh and the stands and the sea of bronze that were in the house of Yahweh, and they carried all of their bronze to Babylon.
And they took away the pots and the shovels and the trimmers and the bowls and the palms and all of the articles of bronze with which they served.
And the basins and the firepans and the bowls and the pots and the lampstands and the palms and the cups that were gold gold and that were silver silver, the chief of the guards took away.

The two pillars, the one sea, and the twelve bronze bulls that were under it and the stands, which King Solomon had made for the house of Yahweh, a weight was not for the bronze of all of these vessels.
And the pillars, 18 cubits was the height of one pillar, and a line of 12 cubits went around it. And its thickness was four fingers. It was hollow.

And the capital upon it was bronze, and the height of one capital was five cubits. And a network and pomegranates were upon the capital all around. The whole was bronze. And like these for the second pillar and the pomegranates.
And 96 pomegranates were to the wind. All of the pomegranates were 100 upon the network all around.
And the chief of the guards took Seraiah, the head priest, and Zephaniah, the priest of the second rank, and the three guards of the threshold.

And from the city he took a eunuch because he was the overseer over the men of war and seven men from the seers of the face of the king who were found in the city and the scribe, the commander of the army, the one mustering the people of the land, and 60 men from the people of the land found in the midst of the city.
And Nebuzaradan, the chief of the guards, took them and made them go to the king of Babylon, to Riblah.
And the king of Babylon struck them and killed them in Riblah in the land of Hamath. And Judah went into exile away from its land.
These are the people whom Nebuchadnezzar exiled. In the year of seven, 3,023 Judeans.
In the year of 18 to Nebuchadnezzar, 832 soul from Jerusalem.
In the year of 23 to Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guards, exiled 745 soul, Judeans. All of the soul was 4,600.

And it happened in year 37 of the exile of Jehoiachin, the king of Judah, in month 12, on 25 of the month, Evil Merodach, the king of Babylon, in the year of his reigning, lifted the head of Jehoiachin, the king of Judah, and he brought him out from the house of imprisonment.
And he spoke good things to him, and he put his seat from above to the seat of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
And he changed the clothes of his imprisonment, and he ate bread regularly to his face all of the days of his life.
And his allowance, a continual allowance, was given to him from the king of Babylon, the matter of a day in its day until the day of his death, all of the days of his life.
